- It is home to more than one million stars.

description: M55 is a dim globular cluster of stars, that never rises high in the sky for Northern observers.
name: Summer Rose Star
trivia: - Discovered in 1752 in South Africa by French astronomer Nicolas Louis de Lacaille, who noted: resembles an obscure nucleus of a big comet.

description: Messier 56 is a globular cluster located very close to the only other Messier object in the constellation of Lyra: the Ring nebula (M57).
name: M56
trivia:
- It only has 1 percent of the Sun’s metallicity.

- It travels in a retrograde orbit in the Milky Way.

description: M57, or the Ring Nebula, is a planetary nebula similar in shape to the bigger Helix nebula. It is one of the faintest objects in the entire Messier Catalog, but is a very popular target for observers and astrophotographers due to its high surface brightness.
name: Ring Nebula
trivia:
- It will faint away in 10,000 years.

- It's growing at a rate of 43,000+ mph.

description: M58 is a barred spiral galaxy that can be found in the Virgo cluster of galaxies. With an apparent magnitude of 10.5, Messier 58 is the brightest member of the Virgo group. It is interesting to note that M58 is the most distant object in the entire Messier catalog!
name: M58
trivia:
- It's one of the very few galaxies that have an ultra-compact nuclear ring.

- One supernova has been detected in the galaxy on January 18, 1988, and a second one on June 28, 1989.

description: In the heart of the Virgo supercluster is the elliptical galaxy Messier 59. M59 is home to a supermassive black hole 100 times more massive than the canter black hole of our Milky Way.
name: M59
trivia:
- M59 contains more than 2,200 globular clusters!

- The region in M59's center rotates in the opposite direction to the rest of the galaxy.

description: The Butterfly cluster is classified as an open cluster. It is located north of the Scorpion's tail and is part of the Milky Way, in direction of the galactic center. The cluster concentrates a hundred stars, mostly young hot blue stars.
name: Butterfly Cluster
trivia:
- Its brightest star is BM Scorpii, an orange giant, whose color contrasts with the multitude of blue stars.

- In the Northern Hemisphere, the best time to observe M6 is in the summer months, by looking towards the south above the horizon. In the Southern Hemisphere, M6 will rise much higher in the sky, during summer and fall.

description: To the very East of the Virgo cluster of galaxies, is Messier 60, a bright giant elliptical galaxy. Not much can be seen when observing or photographing M60, mostly because its brightness, and the type of galaxy it is makes it appear like a blob of light in the sky.
name: M60
trivia:
- M60 is the 3rd brightest elliptical galaxy in the Virgo supercluster, behind M49 and M87.

- It's very close to a spiral galaxy: NGC 4647.

description: Towards the South of the Virgo cluster of galaxies is one of the largest galaxies of the group: the barred spiral galaxy Messier 61. M61 is also classified as a starburst galaxy, as it is forming new stars at a very high speed.
name: M61
trivia: - M61 is the Messier galaxy where the most supernovae have been detected, 7 in the last century.

description: M62 is a globular cluster, not far from M19. Charles Messier discovered the cluster on June 7, 1771, but did not enter it into his catalog until June 4, 1779, because he noted the wrong coordinates during his original discovery.
name: M62
trivia:
- A total of 89 variable stars were discovered in Messier 62.

- In 2013, researchers discovered a stellar-mass black hole in the globular cluster.

description:
M63 is a spiral galaxy located about 37 million light-years away from Earth, it is a member of the M51 group of galaxies.
The Sunflower galaxy got its name from its yellow core and the shape of its arms resembling a sunflower, and is a lot of observers' and astrophotographers' favorite!
name: Sunflower Galaxy
trivia:
- The Sunflower galaxy was Pierre Méchain’s first discovery, in 1779.

- It is one of the first galaxies where a spiral structure was identified.

description: M64, also called the Black Eye galaxy, the Evil Eye galaxy, and the Sleeping Beauty galaxy, is a spiral galaxy lying 24 million light-years away from Earth. Messier 64 is most famous for its dark bands of dust passing in front of its core.
name: Black Eye Galaxy
trivia:
- Getting further away at a speed of 408 km/s.

- Member of the M94 group of galaxies: the Cat’s Eye galaxy group.

- Contains about 100 billion stars.

description: The Leo Triplet is composed of two Messier objects, M65 and M66, as well as NGC 3628, often called the Hamburger galaxy due to its shape. All three galaxies are getting deformed by each other's gravity, but Messier 65 is the one that is the least affected, and looks like a normal spiral galaxy.
name: M65
trivia:
- It is receding from us at about 807 km/s.

- In 2013, a supernova was found in Messier 65.

description: Messier 66 is part of the Leo Triplet, and is the one to the East of the group. It has been deformed by the gravitational pull of its two neighbors, so much that its core is now not in the center of the galaxy anymore.
name: M66
trivia: - Messier 66 is the largest and brightest of the three galaxies forming the Leo Triplet.

description: With an age of between 3 and 5 billion years, Messier 67, in the constellation of Cancer, is the oldest open cluster in the entire Messier Catalog. The stars are expected to disperse in about 5 billion years.
name: King Cobra Cluster
trivia:
- The stars in the King Cobra cluster are around 4 billion years old on average.

- 3 extrasolar planets were discovered in the cluster, in 2014.

description: Messier 68 is a globular cluster in Hydra, and more than 2,000 of its 100,000+ stars are visible from Earth. The cluster is located behind the galactic center and looks like a faint patch of light through binoculars and small instruments.
name: M68
trivia: - Messier 68 probably came from a different galaxy, swallowed by the Milky Way long ago.

description: Near the core of our galaxy lies a beautiful globular cluster, Messier 69. It is also near M70, another globular from the Messier Catalog.
name: M69
trivia:
- M69 is the brightest member of the three Messier globular clusters inside the Teapot asterism.

- In 1784, William Herschel noted that M69 looked like a miniature version of Messier 53.

description: M7 is an open cluster located near the sting of Scorpius. It is one of the closest open clusters of our solar system, it approaches it at a speed of 14 km / s. It concentrates a hundred stars, mostly young blue stars. Messier describes it as a cluster of small stars, among which there is one which has more light.
name: Ptolemy's Cluster
trivia:
- Most stars in the cluster will move away, slowly dissolving the group, while larger stars will explode in novas.

- M7 also bears the name of the one who observed it for the first time in the 2nd century, the Greek astronomer Ptolemy, although he identified it as a nebula.

description: In the Teapot asterism of the Sagittarius constellation is the globular cluster M70. It is the neighbor of two other Messier globulars, M54 and M69. M70 is only 1,800 light-years away from M69.
name: M70
trivia:
- The cluster is a little larger than its 2 neighbors M54 and M69.

- M70 is drifting away at a speed of 200 km/s.

- Alan Hale and Thomas Bopp were looking at M70 when they discovered the now-famous comet Hale-Bopp in 1995.

description: Within the famous Summer Triangle lies M71, a globular cluster with a density classification of X, XI. Messier 71 was once thought to be a very populated cluster, such as M11, but it is actually a very loose object.
name: M71
trivia: - M71 is one of the smallest globular clusters discovered.

description: Similar to Messier 4 and Messier 12, M72 is a pretty faint globular cluster, which can be found in the constellation of Aquarius. M72's age is about 9.5 billion years old and is one of the faintest and smallest objects in Charles Messier's catalog.
name: M72
trivia:
- It is home to at least 43 variable stars.

- It is one of the most remote Messier clusters.

description: Very close to the globular cluster Messier 72, M73 is an asterism formed by 4 stars. It was the third and last of Messier's mistakes, as M73 is not considered to be a deep-sky object.
name: M73
trivia: - Charles Messier thought it was an open cluster, but the 4 stars are not linked by gravity.

description: The Phantom Galaxy is a grand design spiral galaxy, with a large apparent size but a low surface brightness.
name: Phantom Galaxy
trivia:
- It is about the same size as the Milky Way galaxy.

- It's the second galaxy with the lowest surface brightness in the Messier Catalog, after M101.

description: Messier 75 is a dense globular cluster that can be found in the constellation of Sagittarius. It contains about 400,000 stars and lies 47,600 light-years beyond the Milky Way's galactic center.
name: M75
trivia:
- Messier 75 is the most centrally concentrated globular cluster in Messier’s catalog.

- M75 is the most distant Messier globular cluster, after M54, which is not located in our Milky Way galaxy.

description: Also named the Cork nebula or the Barbell nebula, M76 is very similar to M27, the Dumbbell nebula, but appears much smaller. The Little Dumbbell nebula is one of the 4 planetary nebulae in the Messier catalog.
name: Little Dumbbell Nebula
trivia: - Has two designations in the New General Catalogue (NGC 650 and NGC 651) because it was once thought that M76 consisted of two separate emission nebulae.

description: Large and with a bright core, M77 is a barred spiral galaxy in Cetus. It is the central member of the M77 Group, which contains several bound galaxies.
name: Cetus A
trivia: - It's the brightest type 2 Seyfert galaxy in the night sky and one of the most studied galaxies.

description: M78 is located in the constellation of the Hunter: Orion. Messier 78 is a diffuse reflection nebula, near the Orion nebula, the Horsehead and the Flame nebulae.
name: M78
trivia:
- M78 is the brightest diffuse reflection nebula in the night sky.

- It has given life to more than 200 stars.

description: M79 is the second and last extragalactic globular cluster listed in Messier’s catalog, the first one being Messier 54. M79 lies in the constellation of Lepus, and is located in the Canis Major dwarf galaxy, a satellite of ours.
name: M79
trivia:
- Our Milky Way is currently absorbing the Canis Major dwarf galaxy, and it is believed that M79 is being pulled out of it.

- M79 is mostly composed of red giants and blue stars.

description: The Lagoon Nebula is a giant cloud of dust and interstellar gas emitting light in different wavelengths, which explains the richness of its colors (although to the naked eye, it is only visible in gray-green). The nebula is home to bright young stars that give the Lagoon nebula its brilliance, like the giant star Herschel 36, 32 times more massive and 200,000 times brighter than the Sun but hidden by thick clouds of dust.
name: Lagoon Nebula
trivia: To celebrate Hubble's 28th anniversary in 2018, NASA released a spectacular image of the Lagoon Nebula, as well as an immersive video retracing the most important scientific discoveries made by the space telescope.

description: Messier 80 is a globular cluster in the constellation of the Scorpion: Scorpius. It lies just to the northwest of Antares, the brightest star in Scorpius. M80 is not far from another Messier cluster: Messier 4.
name: M80
trivia:
- It's one of the most densely populated globular clusters in the Milky Way.

- A nova was discovered in 1860, it was the first nova ever found in a globular cluster.

description: M81 is a grand design spiral galaxy discovered by Johann Elert Bode in 1774. It is the largest object of the M81 group of galaxies, which contains 34 galaxies in Ursa Major.
name: Bode's Galaxy
trivia:
- It's the farthest large galaxy moving towards the Milky Way known.

- It contains more than 200 globular clusters.

description: In the same field of view as Messier 81 is M82, or the Cigar galaxy, an edge-on starburst galaxy that is about 5 times more luminous than the Milky Way. In 2014, a team of researchers discovered the brightest ever pulsar known inside M82, with a luminosity of 100 times what was thought to be possible.
name: Cigar Galaxy
trivia:
- The Cigar galaxy is the closest starburst galaxy to Earth.

- M81’s tidal forces affect M82 and increase the rate of its star-forming activity.

description: M83 is a barred spiral galaxy in the largest constellation of the night sky: Hydra. The Southern Pinwheel Galaxy is one of the most difficult objects from the Messier catalog to observe because it never rises high above the horizon.
name: Southern Pinwheel Galaxy
trivia:
- It's about half the size of the Milky Way.

- It's one of the closest barred spiral galaxies.

- The galaxy's core is a double nucleus.

description: Messier 84 is a galaxy in Virgo. It is one of the brightest galaxies of the Virgo cluster, and it is also part of Markarian's Chain.
name: M84
trivia: - It is unsure whether Messier 84 is an elliptical galaxy or a lenticular galaxy.

description: Towards the North of the Virgo cluster is M85, a galaxy similar in shape, size and brightness to Messier 84.
name: M85
trivia: - A more visually interesting galaxy is right next to M85, the spiral galaxy NGC 4394.

description: In the same field of view as Messier 84 is another Messier object: M86. It is very similar to its neighbor, and it is also uncertain whether it is an elliptical or a lenticular galaxy.
name: M86
trivia:
- It contains more than 400 billion stars.

- M86 is moving through the Virgo cluster so fast that it is losing a lot of its gas, leaving a trail behind, visible by X-Ray.

description: Messier 87 is a supergiant elliptical galaxy in Virgo. M87 is also called Virgo A, or even the Smoking Gun due to the jet of gas expelling from its core, visible in photographs. M87 has an impressive total mass of 2.7 trillion solar masses.
name: Virgo A
trivia:
- It is about the same size as the Milky Way galaxy.

- M87 is one of the brightest and largest galaxies in the local universe.

description: M88 is a beautiful, slightly inclined spiral galaxy that looks like a small, purple Andromeda galaxy.
name: M88
trivia: - It's one of the 15 Messier objects located in the Virgo cluster.

description: Messier 89 is an elliptical galaxy part of the Virgo Cluster. M89 is very round, which is rare for ellipticals, as they often have a slight oval shape.
name: M89
trivia: - It is believed to contain about 10 times as many globular clusters than the Milky Way.

description: Messier 9 is a star cluster located in the southern part of the constellation of Ophiuchus. It is the nearest globular cluster to the galactic center, with a distance of 5,500 light-years. Its age is estimated at 12 billion years, almost as old as the Universe itself. The cluster concentrates many of the oldest stars of the Universe, 13 variable stars and many red giants (the destiny of our Sun at the end of its life).
name: M9
trivia:
- M9 is speeding away from us at a speed of 200km per second!

- The best time to observe M9 is in summer.

description: M90 is a spiral galaxy, near several other Messier objects where the Virgo cluster is located. Messier 90 is in the process of slowly turning into a lenticular galaxy.
name: M90
trivia: - Companion galaxy IC 3583 can be seen when observing M90, but most likely will become farther and farther from its neighbor in the future.

description: Messier 91 is one of the most difficult Messier objects to observe in the night sky, because of its magnitude and size. Photographing the galaxy will allow you to see the bar that makes it a barred spiral galaxy, but it is extremely difficult to see it visually.
name: M91
trivia: - It's the faintest object in the entire Messier catalog.

description: M92 is a globular cluster, similar to the famous Hercules Globular Cluster (M13) but smaller and fainter. Both clusters also lie in the same constellation.
name: M92
trivia: - Messier 92 is as old as the Universe itself, and may be the oldest globular cluster in the entire Milky Way.

description: Near Sirius, the brightest star in the night sky, is an open cluster, Messier 93. The cluster contains hundreds of stars, although only about 80 were confirmed.
name: M93
trivia: - In apparent size, it's about two-thirds the size of the full moon.

description: Messier 94 is a beautiful spiral galaxy, that has the shape of a feline's eye. M94 is part of the Canes Venatici I Cloud, which is home to about 20 galaxies, including the Black Eye galaxy. Messier 94 is the brightest one of the group.
name: Cat’s Eye Galaxy
trivia:
- It is also called the Cat’s Eye galaxy or Croc’s Eye galaxy.

- It is drifting away from Earth at a speed of 308 km/s.

description: Messier 95 is a barred spiral galaxy that is part of the M96 galaxy group (also known as the Leo I Group). M95 has a magnitude of 11.4, and is simply impossible to spot with the naked eye. It is also extremely difficult to see with binoculars.
name: M95
trivia:
- It's drifting away from the Milky Way at 778 km/s .

- It's one of the faintest objects in the Messier catalog.

- M95 contains about 40 billion stars.

description:
M96 is considered an intermediate spiral galaxy, and just like M95, it is part of the Leo I Group of galaxies. The group is made up of more than 12 galaxies, including three Messier objects.
Astronomers found that there was a greater concentration of dust in the right side of the galaxy, and deducted that the right side of M96 was closer to Earth than the left.
name: M96
trivia:
- It's receding from the Milky Way at 897 km/s.

- It's the brightest and largest member of the M96 group.

- It contains about 100 billion stars.

description: Messier 97 is found in the constellation of Ursa Major just under the bright star Merak. The Owl nebula is a very small, faint, and unimpressive object, but it is a popular target for astrophotographers. The main reason being it lies near the Surfboard galaxy, or M108.
name: Owl Nebula
trivia:
- It is very similar to the Southern Owl nebula in size, shape, and color.

- It got the name of Owl nebula after William Parsons’ drawing from 1848.

description: M98 is an intermediate spiral galaxy that is part of the Virgo Cluster. It has a very low surface brightness and is one of the faintest objects in the Messier catalog, making it a difficult target to observe.
name: M98
trivia: - It contains about a trillion stars and is drifting towards us at a speed of 142 km/s.

description: Messier 99, or the Coma Pinwheel galaxy, is a member of the large Virgo Cluster. The galaxy has an asymmetric shape similar to M101, the regular Pinwheel galaxy.
name: Coma Pinwheel
trivia:
- M99 has one normal spiral arm, and one that appears distorted

- The galaxy's nucleus is not exactly in the center due to repeated interactions with other nearby galaxies.

description: Mars is the 4th planet orbiting our Sun, and it is most likely the next place where humans will set foot! Mars is a rocky planet with about one-third the gravity of Earth. One day on the planet is just a little over 24 hours, but one year is much longer than an on Earth, with 687 days!
name: Mars
trivia:
- Mars has two moons, Phobos and Deimos.

- Mars is often called the Red Planet because the iron minerals in its soil make the Martian atmosphere look red.

- The first mission to Mars to succeed was in 1965, with the Mariner 4 flyby.

description:
The Hyades, also known as Melotte 25, is an open cluster located in the constellation Taurus. The name of the cluster comes from the Rain Nymphs, daughter of Atlas and half-sister of the Pleiades. It is the closest open cluster to us with an estimated distance of only 150 light years. It contains at least 515 stars and is about 800 million years old. When the cluster was formed its total mass must have been about 1,500 times the mass of the Sun. But since then, the cluster has lost mass. Some of the most massive stars have died, the mass has been dispersed by dynamical interactions and some stars are regularly ejected from the cluster. Among the remaining stars, the most massive are about 2.5 times heavier than the Sun. We also note the presence of some white dwarfs, a residual type of star, as the Sun will become.
The cluster has a size in the sky of 5°. Mosaic mode is recommended for this observation.
name: Hyades
trivia:
The cluster is close in the sky to Aldebaran but this star is not part of the open cluster. Aldebaran is located closer to us.
In ancient Greece, the return of the Hyades cluster in the sky was associated with the beginning of the rainy season. The heliacal rising being the moment when the stars rise above the horizon in the East.
Albert Einstein's theory predicts that masses must distort space-time which must modify the path of light. This prediction was verified in 1919 by Arthur Eddington. During the total solar eclipse of May 29, he observed the displacement of the positions of the stars of the Hyades cluster.

description:
The Coma Star Cluster, known as Melotte 111 or Collinder 256, is an open cluster in the Coma Berenices constellation. It should not be confused with the Coma Cluster (Abell 1656), which is a cluster of galaxies also found in the Coma Berenices constellation.
At an estimated distance of only 280 light-years, the open cluster is the second closest open cluster to us after Hyades. The cluster formed about 600 million years ago and studies have currently identified more than 330 members.
name: Coma Star Cluster
trivia:
In ancient history, the cluster was used to define the tail of the Leo constellation. Ptolemy decided to create the Coma Berenices constellation and associate the cluster with it.

There are as many stars in the cluster as there were seats in the 1889 House of Representatives.

description: Mercury is the smallest and closest planet to the Sun in our Solar System, and if you were to walk on its rocky surface, the sun would look three times bigger than the way we see it on Earth. Two missions were sent to Mercury, Mariner 10 in 1974 and Messenger, which went into the planet's orbit in 2011.
name: Mercury
trivia:
- It's the smallest and closest planet to the Sun in our Solar System.

- One day and one night on Mercury take 175.97 days on Earth, but a full year on the small planet is only 88 days on Earth!

- Mercury does not have any moon or rings.

description:
Mira is a star in the constellation of the Whale. Its Latin name was given by the astronomer Johannes Hevelius in 1662. It means the wonderful or the surprising. This is because Mira A has the specific characteristic of being a variable star, its brightness can vary up to 8 magnitudes over a period of 333 days even though the cycle is irregular. To the naked eye, the star appears red and very bright before disappearing in the most extreme cases.
However, using more sophisticated instruments, astronomers have discovered that the star is a binary system consisting of a red giant star (Mira A) and a white dwarf (Mira B). The variation of luminosity observed is only related to Mira A.
The origin of this variability is due to regular charging of the properties inside the star. With its advanced age, the heart of the star is composed of carbon and oxygen which does not burn and therefore no longer produces photons. Above this core there is a small shell of burning helium and above this, a shell of burning hydrogen. These nuclear reactions produce photons that make the star grow. As it grows, the luminosity of the star decreases. The temperature also drops and the nuclear reactions stop. Without these reactions, the star contracts, the luminosity increases, the temperature also increases and the reactions start again, creating a new cycle.
name: Mira
trivia:
Mira is the first variable star discovered that was neither a nova nor a supernova, the only variable stars known at the time. It was therefore used to define a new type of variable star, the Mira. These are red giant stars whose luminosity varies over periods of a few hundred days.

In a hundred thousand years, the Mira A star will evolve into a planetary nebula.

The star loses the equivalent of the mass of Mars each year due to its stellar winds

description: The Moon is our planet's only permanent natural satellite, and was formed 4.51 billion years ago. From Earth, we can only see the same side of the Moon because it is in synchronous rotation with our planet. Our satellite makes a full orbit around Earth in 29.5 days.
name: Moon
trivia:
- It's the 5th largest natural satellite in our Solar System.

- This is the only other body where humans have set foot… 6 times.

description:
Mu Cephei, also known as Herschel's Garnet Star or Erakis, is a red supergiant star in the constellation Cepheus. It is located on the edge of the Elephant’s Trunk nebula, which will give a red color to a portion of the background sky in the image. This red-looking star in the sky, as noted by astronomer William Herschel, has a surface temperature of 3,475°C. This is more than twice the temperature needed to melt cast iron. Its radius is estimated to be about 1,200 times that of our Sun, making it one of the 15 largest stars known. If we replaced the Sun with this star, its surface would be located between the orbit of Jupiter and Saturn.
Weighing 25 times the mass of the Sun at birth, the star loses the equivalent of the mass of the Earth each year. Having burned the hydrogen in its core, the current temperature of over 100 million degrees is now high enough for the helium to fuse and transform into carbon. The hydrogen in the layers surrounding the nucleus is transformed into helium.
name: Herschel's Garnet Star
trivia: On Earth, Alpha Ursae Minoris, also known as the North Star, is used to identify the North. On Mars, Mu Cephei is the star that indicates the North.

description: Napoleon's Hat, also known as Picot 1, is an asterism in the Bootes constellation. The group of stars near Arcturus resembles the famous “bicorne” (two-pointed hat) of the emperor of the French Napoleon. The asterism was discovered in 1995 by the amateur astronomer Fulbert Picot.
name: Napoleon's Hat
trivia: On August 8, 1769, a week before Napoleon was born, Charles Messier discovered a comet that would later become visible to the naked eye. At the end of his life, Messier named this celestial body Napoleon’s Comet to curry favor with the emperor. Back then, the passage of a comet was seen as an important event marking the beginning of a new era.

description: Neptune is an ice giant, and the 8th planet from the Sun. It has 13 moons, named after sea gods and nymphs from the Greek mythology. The planet also has 6 confirmed rings. Just like Uranus, the planet was never studied from up close, and Voyager 2 was the only spacecraft to ever fly by it.
discoveredBy: Urbain Le Verrier, John Couch Adams, Johann Galle
name: Neptune
trivia:
- Neptune is the windiest planet in our solar system.

- It is believed that Neptune has one more moon, and it is currently awaiting confirmation.

description: NGC 1023, also known as the Perseus Lenticular Galaxy, is, as its name suggests, a lenticular-type galaxy in the Perseus constellation. It has a diameter of 57,000 light-years, in other words, nearly half the size of the Milky Way. Its center contains a supermassive black hole of 44 million solar masses. The galaxy has almost already consumed all of its gas and can no longer form new stars. The stars are actually mostly old, which gives the image a yellow-orange color. On the disk, note the presence of rare young clusters with blue stars.
name: Perseus Lenticular Galaxy
trivia: Not bright enough for your instrument, researchers detected a dwarf galaxy in orbit around NGC 1023. Because this satellite galaxy still forms stars, it appears blue.

description: With an apparent size similar to the full moon, 47 Tucanae is the second largest, but also brightest globular cluster in the night sky. In May 2015, researchers showed the first evidence of dynamic mass segregation happening inside the globular cluster.
name: 47 Tucanae
trivia:
- 47 Tucanae was first believed to be a simple star instead of a globular cluster, and so it was catalogued as the 47th star in Tucana.

- Outshone only by the enormous NGC 5139: Omega Centauri.

description: Located in Cetus, about 45 million light-years from the Milky Way, NGC 1055 is a barred spiral galaxy seen from the edge. Reminiscent of the most famed Sombrero galaxy, it is distinguished by its central bulb and its very marked dust lanes, dense obscuring bands of interstellar dust.
name: NGC 1055
trivia:
- Although we see galaxies NGC1073 and NGC 1055 differently, they have the same type of structure: their spiral arms do not emerge from the center of the galaxy, but from a band of stars crossing their center. 
The galaxy NGC 1055 is 30% larger than NGC 1073.

description: NGC 1073 is a barred spiral galaxy located in Cetus, the fourth largest constellation in the sky. It is part of a group of 7 galaxies (including M77 and NGC 1055) whose average distance from the Milky Way is estimated at 55 million light-years.
name: NGC 1073
trivia:
- Although we see galaxies NGC1073 and NGC 1055 differently, they have the same type of structure: their spiral arms do not emerge from the center of the galaxy, but from a band of stars crossing their center. 
The galaxy NGC 1073 is 30% smaller than NGC 1055.

description:
NGC 1097, also known as Caldwell 67, is a spiral galaxy in the Fornax constellation.
The central black hole at the heart of this galaxy weighs 140 million solar masses. Stretching out from the central bulge is a bar-like structure from which two spiral arms emerge. The spiral arms are considerably distorted by interactions with a satellite galaxy. Matter from the outer part is attracted toward the inner parts of the galaxy creating a ring 5,000 light-years from the center. This area is conducive to new star formation.
name: NGC 1097
trivia: Three supernova explosions were detected in this galaxy. The first was in 1992, the second in 1999, and the third in 2003. All three were due to the explosive end of a massive star’s life.

description:
NGC 1232 is a spiral galaxy in the Eridanus constellation.
From a virtually face-on view, it presents well defined spiral arms that are illuminated by numerous stars. In the central areas, the old stars emit the yellow-orange color, while in the outer areas, the young stars emit the blue colors. Its size is between that of our galaxy and that of Andromeda.
Slightly detached from the arms, note the presence of a small diffuse luminous spot. It is a satellite galaxy of NGC 1232.
name: NGC 1232
trivia:
NGC 1232 is a good illustration of what our galaxy should look like.

The galaxy is moving away from us at a speed of 1,600 km/s. This means in just one second, it covers the distance traveled by an airliner in two hours.

description: NGC 1245 is an open cluster in the Perseus constellation. According to Gaia Mission results, the cluster contains at least 479 1.2-billion-year-old stars in a sphere less than 40 light-years in diameter. Comparatively, within a radius of 20 light-years around the Sun, there are less than 100 known stars. The cluster also contains 5 blue straggler stars, which are warmer and brighter than the rest of their companions. They are not cluster members but rather foreground stars. The whole thing is approaching us at 30 km/s. The two bright stars in the middle of the image however are HD 20023 and HD 20077.
name: NGC 1245
trivia:
The cluster is sometimes called the Patrick Starfish Cluster in reference to the cartoon character SpongeBob SquarePants.

There are 30 more stars in the cluster than there are rock paintings in the Chauvet Cave, one of the oldest known decorated caves.

description:
Situated just 230 million light-years away, NGC 1275, also known as Perseus A, lies tucked away within the sprawling northern Perseus constellation.
This stellar island ranks among the nearest giant elliptical galaxies and most powerful source of steady radio emissions in the entire sky.
Appearing as a condensed snowball with circular halos through telescopes, this cosmic titan, spans some 100,000 light years across and also happens to be the brightest member within a massive collection of galaxies called the Perseus cluster.
NGC 1275 lies at the center of this cluster some 275 million light years away. The cluster is considered one of the most massive objects in the Universe containing thousands of galaxies within a diameter of about 12 million light years.
name: Perseus A
trivia: Beyond its sizable radio emissions, NGC 1275 stands out as a significant generator of powerful X-rays. This radiation originates from the galaxy's core, where a supermassive black hole exists with a mass around 800 million times that of the Sun. The X-rays are a result of the friction and various forces generated by spiralling gas as it plunges into the gravitational maw of the feeding black hole.

description:
NGC 1313 is a barred spiral galaxy visible in Reticulum, a faint constellation in the southern sky. This active galaxy is part of the starburst galaxy classification as indicated by its huge amount of oxygen-rich nebulae and its massive young stars population. 
 
The heterogeneous or the asymmetric spiral arms visible in NGC 1313 suggest a past chaotic milestone; for example a potential collision with another galaxy. This hypothesis is still under scrutiny. One main source of doubt is that as NGC 1313 is a field galaxy; therefore it is wandering in the interstellar medium and gravitational interaction with other galaxies is unlikely.
name: Topsy Turvy Galaxy
trivia:
- NGC 1313 is fascinating in many aspects. Its rotation axis, around which the whole galaxy is orbiting, does not match the center of the spiral, which reinforces the idea that it may be the result of a galactic merger.

75 to 90% of the UV light it emits does not come from the usual strong sources such as star clusters but from isolated stars. This observation, carried out by Hubble, confirms that dying star clusters can eject parts of their populations and disseminate them within a galaxy.

In 2015, the discovery of an ultraluminous X-ray source at its center proved the existence of an intermediate-mass black hole of 5,000 solar masses called NGC 1313 X-1.

description: The Fornax Cluster, also known as ACO S373, is a cluster of galaxies primarily located in the Fornax constellation with partial spillover into the Eridanus. It is the second richest cluster of galaxies within 100 million light-years of us. The cluster contains more than 500 galaxies with a total mass of 70,000 billion times the mass of the Sun. It is divided into two subgroups centered on the elliptical galaxy NGC 1399 for the first, and on the lenticular galaxy NGC 1316, for the second. NGC 1316 is also the biggest and brightest galaxy in the group. On the image, centered on NGC 1316, a significant portion of the yellow-orange points are not stars, they are galaxies
name: Fornax Cluster (NGC 1316)
trivia:
If the Sun had the mass of an ant, the total mass of the cluster would be equivalent to 10 blue whales.

NGC 1316 is likely the result of a merger of several smaller galaxies. A portion of the mass of each of the smaller galaxies would likely have fed the central black hole to make it grow up to 150 million solar masses.

description: The Robin’s Egg Nebula, also known as NGC 1360, is a planetary nebula in the Fornax constellation. 10,000 years ago, a dying star created this nebula that expanded into the interstellar medium. Its current shape resembles a rugby ball the size of which is about 3 light-years in length. The material of the nebula has begun to merge and mix with the interstellar medium. The blue color in the image is caused by the presence of oxygen in the nebula. Being heated by the remnant star, it emits light in this band of color. The central star is a system consisting of two white dwarfs. The mass of each of the stars is estimated to be ⅔ that of the current Sun and their temperature over 100,000°C.
name: Robin's Egg Nebula
trivia:
The identity of the nebula’s discoverer is a complicated affair. Some sources indicate that it was Friedrich Winnecke in 1868. Lewis Swift is however said to have observed it in 1859 but only published his results in 1885. Finally, Wilhelm Tempel would have likely made the observation on October 9, 1861.

When the planetary nebula formed, several species disappeared from the Earth, such as the woolly mammoth, saber-tooth tiger, cave bear, and cave lion.

description: NGC 1365 is a double-barred spiral galaxy that can be found in the constellation Fornax. It is located 56 millions light-years away and has a magnitude of 9,6. Due to its shape, it is also called The Great Spiral Galaxy.
name: Great Barred Spiral Galaxy
trivia: - The Great Spiral Galaxy is part of the Fornax galaxy cluster, the NGC 1316 group, which includes more than 20 galaxies.

description: The Fornax Cluster, also known as ACO S373, is a cluster of galaxies primarily located in the Fornax constellation with partial spillover into the Eridanus. It is the second richest cluster of galaxies within 100 million years of us. The cluster contains more than 500 galaxies with a total mass of 70,000 billion times the mass of the Sun. It is divided into two subgroups centered on the elliptical galaxy NGC 1399 for the first, and on the lenticular galaxy NGC 1316, for the second. NGC 1316 is also the biggest and brightest galaxy in the group. On the image, centered on NGC 1399, a significant portion of the yellow-orange points are not stars, they are galaxies
name: Fornax Cluster (NGC 1399)
trivia:
- If the Sun had the mass of an ant, the total mass of the cluster would be equivalent to 450 blue whales.

- NGC 1316 is likely the result of a merger of several smaller galaxies. A portion of the mass of each of the smaller galaxies would likely have fed the central black hole to make it grow up to 150 million solar masses.

- NGC 1399 contains about 6,000 globular clusters. A portion of these were likely torn from the neighboring galaxy NGC 1404. The galaxy also contains 37 planetary nebulae.

description: NGC 147, also known as Caldwell 17, is a dwarf galaxy in the Cassiopeia constellation. The galaxy resembles an American football with a length of 11,000 light-years and a width of 7,500 light-years. The total mass of the galaxy is estimated to be 55 million times that of the Sun. The galaxy is in fact a satellite of the Andromeda Galaxy M31. The stars in the galaxy formed more than 3 billion years ago. There seems to be no gas left in the galaxy and the interstellar medium is empty. The galaxy can no longer form new stars.
name: NGC 147
trivia: NGC 147 is also linked by gravity to the galaxy NGC 185, which is also a satellite galaxy of the Andromeda Galaxy.

description: NGC 1491, also known as SH 2-206, is an emission nebula in the Perseus constellation. Unlike many emission nebulae, this region of gas and dust is not heated by a nearby open cluster but by a single star. Named BD +50° 886, it is a massive star that represents 40 solar masses. Its surface temperature is 45,000°C. Its luminosity is 350,000 times that of our star. The matter expelled from the star will accelerate to several hundred km/s and ram and compress the gas in the interstellar medium that surrounds it. The photons emitted by the star will heat the interstellar medium.
name: SH 2-206
trivia: If the star that makes the nebula shine were to replace our Sun, its surface would exceed the orbit of Saturn.

description: The California nebula is an emission nebula from the Perseus constellation. It is only 1000 light-years away, located in the Orion Arm, a minor spiral arm of the Milky Way galaxy. Of an apparent magnitude of 6, its red color reflects a strong presence of hydrogen.
name: California Nebula
trivia:
- It is named after the State of California in the United States as its shape resembles it.
- To find the California nebula, use the Pleiades as a reference as they are in the same direction.
- Stretching over a distance of about 100 light-years, it is necessary to have a very wide field instrument to be able to photograph it in full.

description: Kemble's Cascade is a famous asterism visible in the constellation of the Giraffe: Camelopardalis. It was named in honor of Lucien Kemble, who wrote about the asterism as a beautiful cascade of stars.
name: Kemble's Cascade
trivia: - Kemble's Cascade is made up of more than 20 faint stars. The shape of the asterism points to the constellation Cassiopeia.

description:
NGC 1555, also referred to as Hind's Variable Nebula, Sh2-238, or HH 155, is a dynamic nebula 400 light years from Earth, nestled within the borders of Taurus, the bull constellation.
The discovery of this nebula dates back to October 11, 1852, credited to the keen eye of John Russell Hind. As its name suggests this 4 light year diameter gas cloud actually changes its shape and brightness thanks to the nearby variable star called T Tauri that is embedded in dust and gas. But T Tauri is actually composed of three, very young individual stars very close together, with one believed to still be at its earliest stages of formation.
name: Hind's Variable Nebula
trivia: Turns out that both nebula and variable star are part of a much larger stream of star-forming region known as the Taurus-Auriga complex, containing one of the nearest group of young stars to our Solar System, all younger than 2 million years.

description: NGC 1579 is a diffuse nebula in the Perseus Constellation, also called the Northern Trifid because of its similarity to M20. The color of this region of ionized hydrogen, known as the HII region (as in H2), is mainly due to its gas being excited by radiation from the star LkHα 101. This 15 solar mass star is part of a young cluster, about 1 million years old, in which stars are still forming. In addition to LkH α 101, 5 other stars larger than 10 solar masses have been detected.
name: Northern Trifid
trivia: The distance to the cluster and the exact nature of LkHα 101 are difficult to determine and highly uncertain. Numerous studies have been undertaken and the findings range from 160 to 800 parsecs, or 600 to 1,600 light years.

description: NGC 1761 is an open cluster located in the constellation Dorado, a small and fainted constellation whose stars do not exceed magnitude 3. Cluster NGC 1761 has an apparent magnitude between 9 and 10. The cluster is located in the Large Cloud of Magellan, in the N11 region, home to several nebulae and open star clusters.
name: NGC 1761
trivia: - The object is more easily visible from the southern hemisphere.

description:
Tucked away in a dark region of the famed Orion, the hunter Constellation is the delicate cosmic cloud called NGC 1788.
Found not too far beyond the bright star Rigel, this isolated dusty cocoon is known as a reflection nebula - a type of cloud of gas and dust that appears to shine thanks to scattering light radiating out from a nearby cluster of stars. While the nebulosity overall appearance is compact and elongated it is contained within a keystone configuration of four stars, the brightest of which is only 10th magnitude.
Look for an almost round, central bright core that is wrapped in wispy filaments stretching out into surrounding dark expanse of interstellar space.
name: NGC 1788
trivia: Every star in this region is super young, averaging just a million years old—basically a cosmic blink of an eye! To put it in perspective, our Sun has been around for a whopping 4.5 billion years, while the stars associated with NGC 1788 are like cosmic toddlers compared to the Sun's grandparent status.

description: NGC 185, also known as Caldwell 18, is a dwarf galaxy in the Cassiopeia constellation. Looking like a flattened balloon, it measures between 10,000 and 12,000 light-years in diameter for a weight of 660 million Suns. The galaxy is in fact a satellite of the Andromeda Galaxy M31. The stars in the outer reaches of the galaxy formed more than a billion years ago. In the central regions, however, the galaxy still seems to be forming new stars as demonstrated by the presence of young star clusters.
name: NGC 185
trivia: NGC 185 is also linked by gravity to the galaxy NGC 147, which is also a satellite galaxy of the Andromeda Galaxy.

description: NGC 1851, also known as Caldwell 73, is a globular cluster in the constellation Columba. The mass of the cluster is estimated to be 550,000 times the mass of the Sun, spread over an estimated 200,000 stars. This number of stars is equivalent to the brown bear population in the world. The stars in the cluster are about 10 billion years old and did not all form at the same time. Two different populations were identified with very old, red stars and younger, more massive, hotter, blue stars. Researchers are trying to understand how these two populations came to be.
name: NGC 1851
trivia: NGC 1851 is part of the Gaia Sausage with 7 other globular clusters. Using data from the Gaia satellite, it has been shown that NGC 1851, as well as M 2, M 56, M 75, M 79, NGC 2298, NGC 5286, and NGC 2808 formed in a dwarf galaxy. Eventually, this galaxy was absorbed into the Milky Way and the clusters mixed with the star populations of our galaxy.

description: NGC 188 is located in the constellation Cepheus and is circumpolar, meaning it is so close to the North Celestial Pole that it is above the horizon at all times from anywhere in the Northern Hemisphere. It is estimated to be over 4 billion years old, making it one of the oldest open clusters known in the Milky Way.
name: NGC 188
trivia: - NGC 188 is also known as Caldwell 1, the first object in the Caldwell catalog.

description: IC 2118 is a reflection nebula in Eridan, illuminated by the bright star Rigel. This nebula is pretty faint but also very large. It got its nickname of Witch Head Nebula as in photographs, the nebula looks like the profile of a witch. IC 2118 was discovered by William Herschel in 1786.
name: Witch Head Nebula
trivia: - Molecular clouds and star-forming regions have been found in some parts of the Witch Head Nebula through observations made in the field of radio waves. Tauri-type stars and main pre-sequence stars have also been detected.

description: The Fly Nebula, also known as NGC 1931, is an open cluster embedded in an emission and reflection nebula in the Auriga constellation. A massive star of about 8 solar masses formed in the region 25 million years ago. Its intense radiation causes the surrounding nebulae to glow either blue when the light is simply reflected or red if it is absorbed and re-emitted by the gas. The gas and dust region was disrupted and new young stars less than 2 million years old are forming.
name: Fly Nebula
trivia:
When the star formed 25 million years ago, the ancestor of the wombat, the animal with cube-shaped excrements, the Mukupirna nambensis, walked the Earth. The ancestor weighed about 150 kg, the size of a black bear.

At less than 1° in the sky but 10,000 light-years in the galaxy, is the Spider Nebula, IC 417.

description: NGC 1955 is a star cluster associated with an emission nebula found in the Dorado constellation, more precisely, near the Large Magellanic Cloud, and only visible from the Southern Hemisphere. This is a region called H II (read H 2, characterized by very extensive, hydrogen charged clouds; most of its atoms are ionized (modified atomic structure) when they come into contact with the clusters' stars.
name: NGC 1955

description: The Running Man Nebula is a cloud of interstellar gas and dust located in the constellation Orion, in the Hunter's Sword area. Unlike its neighbor the Orion M42 nebula, this object is dominated by blue colors coming from interstellar dust reflecting the light emitted by hot young stars from this region.
name: Running Man Nebula
trivia:
- It's said that the nebula's name comes from a group of American amateur astronomers to whom the X-shaped dark bands think of a running man. Since then, the nickname has spread widely.

- NGC1977 is the neighbor of two smaller nebulae: NGC 1973 and NGC 1975.

description: NGC 2014 is an emission nebula associated with a star cluster found in the constellation Dorado and more precisely, in the region of the Large Magellanic Cloud, visible only from the Southern Hemisphere. Called stellar nurseries, emission nebulae are home to stars so massive and energetic that they sculpt the envelope of gas and dust that surrounds them.
name: NGC 2014
trivia: - NGC 2014 is the neighbor of the nebula NGC 2020. The duo, called the cosmic reef, was imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope for its 30th anniversary.

description: Detected in photographs in 1888, along with the Horsehead nebula and NGC 2023, the Flame nebula is an emission nebula that is part of the Orion Molecular Cloud Complex. A cluster of young, still forming stars is present in the center of the Flame, but is not actually visible to amateur observers.
name: Flame Nebula
trivia: - The gases in the Flame nebula shine thanks to the bright star Alnitak.

description: The Tarantula nebula is a huge, bright object located in the Large Magellanic Cloud, outside of the Milky Way galaxy. The nebula is so huge and bright that if it were as close to us as the famous Orion nebula, you would be able to see your shadows when it rises in the sky. The nebula was discovered by the French astronomer Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille while he was traveling to the Cape of Good Hope.
name: Tarantula Nebula
trivia:
- A Supernova was found around the edges of the Tarantula Nebula in 1987. This is the closest supernova ever discovered since the invention of the telescope.

- The Tarantula nebula is one of the largest, brightest, and is most active starburst region in our Local Group.

description:
NGC 2141 is a rich open cluster hiding out in the constellation Orion’s raised club. Discovered by American astronomer Edward Barnard in 1883, it resides at a distance of approximately 13,200 light years from our Solar System.
Its age, estimated at 1.7 billion years, is complemented by an apparent size in the sky equivalent to one-third of the moon's disk, while its actual size in space spans about 38.3 light years. Unlike many young star clusters throughout the Milky Way, NGC 2141 mysteriously lacks an abundance of youthful blue stars, and instead showcases a nearly equal blend with red stars, which may indicate the cluster gravitationally may have captured, foreign stars and incorporated them into the cluster.
This celestial gathering is not only a captivating sight but also strategically positioned near the celestial equator. As a result, observers from both Northern and Southern hemispheres can enjoy glimpses of its stellar splendours.
name: NGC 2141
trivia: Astronomers speculate that the reddening in some of the member stars in NGC 2141 may in fact be due to the starlight shining through the nebulosity found spread throughout the Orion constellation region. This starlight travels through layers of gas and dust left behind by an ancient supernova shifts its light towards the red part of the light spectrum before reaching Earth.

description:
The Little Pleiades, also known as NGC 2169, is an open cluster in the Orion constellation. The cluster is sometimes called the 37 Cluster because the stars appear to form that number in the sky.

According to the most recent data from the Gaia Mission, the cluster consists of at least 65 stars. The stars are estimated to be 9 million years old. They are moving away from us at a speed of 100,000 km/h, that is, 3.5 times faster than the ISS.
name: Little Pleiades
trivia: When the NGC 2169 stars formed 9 million years ago, a species of monkey, Rudapithecus hungaricus, was beginning to stand upright and walk on its two hind legs. This discovery was made by anthropologists while studying the fossilized bones of a specimen found in Rudabánya, Hungary.

description: NGC 2174 is an emission nebula associated with a star cluster that can be found in the Orion constellation, above the red supergiant star Betelgeuse. Located about 6400 light-years from Earth, it is 4 times farther away than its neighbor the Orion Nebula. We can also see, in front of the gas cloud of the nebula, the young star cluster NGC 2175 whose age is estimated at 9 million years.
name: Monkey Head Nebula
trivia: - In 2014, the Hubble Space Telescope released a new image mosaic of a closer look part of NGC 2174 to celebrate its 24th anniversary. It allowed the N/ASA & ESA teams to demonstrate Hubble's powerful infrared vision, offering a hint of what scientists can expect from the upcoming James Webb Space Telescope.

description: The Rosette nebula is a beautiful object in Monoceros that is very difficult to see visually. It is home to a young cluster of stars, NGC 2244, that formed within the gases a million years ago. This cluster is, unlike the nebula itself, very easy to spot in the night sky and you may even be able to see it without any instrument. The Rosette nebula is massive, colorful, and full of details, which makes it a fantastic target to photograph.
name: Rosette Nebula
trivia:
- It was discovered in 5 different parts over time.

- It is sometimes called “The Skull”.

- It's one of the most massive known emission nebulae.

description: NGC 2261 was the targeted object for the Hale telescope's first light at Mount Palomar observatory on January 26, 1949, 20 years after it began construction in 1928. It was Edwin Hubble who manipulated the telescope. He had previously studied the nebula at Yerkes Observatory and Mount Wilson Observatory.
name: Hubble's Variable Nebula
trivia: - NGC 2261 lies about 2,500 light-years away from the solar system and it extends about 2.2 light-years at its maximum size. It is lit by R Monocerotis, a variable star of type T Tauri. The variable brightness of NGC 2261 does not only come from the variable brightness of R Mon. A proposed model evokes dense dust clouds that periodically obstruct light from the star.

description: Located in the constellation Monoceros (the Unicorn), NGC2264 actually designates two astronomical objects: the Cone, a diffuse nebula located in the south, and the Christmas Tree, a young star cluster located in the north. NGC2264's brightest star is S Monocerotis.
name: Cone nebula / Christmas Tree cluster
trivia:
- The nebula takes its name from the conical shape of the object, a giant pillar composed of gas and interstellar dust. It is similar to the Pillars of Creation located in the Eagle Nebula. 
- The inverted triangular shape of the cluster evokes the outline of a Christmas tree.

description: NGC 2281 is an open cluster in the Auriga constellation. The latest studies based on data from the Gaia mission have confirmed that at least 400 stars belong to the cluster. Unlike many open clusters, there does not appear to be a concentration of stars in the center of the cluster. This one is 650 million years old. Consequently, stars three times more massive than the Sun are already dead.
name: NGC 2281
trivia: When NGC 2281 stars were forming, Earth was in the Marinoan glaciation period. Earth would have been a huge snowball entirely covered by ice.

description:
NGC 2298 is a globular cluster in the Puppis constellation. The first stars in this cluster formed 12.7 billion years ago. Currently, the mass of this cluster is estimated to be 50,000 times that of the Sun. It decreases regularly because the cluster is breaking apart and losing stars. It has already lost 85% of its original mass, and the ejected stars form what is called a tidal tail; a kind of filament attached to the cluster. This structure is not visible on the image. 
The stars in the cluster are moving away from us at a speed of 147 km/s or 529,200 km/h. In other words, the stars are moving 500 times faster than an airliner.
name: NGC 2298
trivia: NGC 2298, along with seven other globular clusters, is part of the Gaia Sausage. As revealed by Gaia Mission data, NGC 2298 and M2, M56, M75, M79, NGC 1851, NGC 5286, and NGC 2808 formed in a dwarf galaxy. This galaxy was subsequently absorbed by the Milky Way and the clusters mixed with the star populations of our Galaxy.

description: Thor’s Helmet is a cloud of interstellar gas that has the shape of Thor’s Helmet. Although it is a faint target and is not really impressive when observing, the colors in the gases really pop when taking long exposure shots with a camera. This beautiful deep-sky object gets its glow from WR7, a massive Wolf-Rayet star that will soon turn into a supernova.
name: Thor's Helmet
trivia:
- A Wolf-Rayet star within the gases gives NGC 2359 its glow.

- It is similar to the Bubble nebula, but much more complex.

description:
NGC 2360, also known as Caroline's Cluster, is an open star cluster located in the constellation Canis Major, approximately 3,700 light-years away from Earth.

This cluster contains approximately 60 relatively young stars, with an estimated age of around 60 million years.
name: Caroline's Cluster
trivia:
The cluster was discovered in 1783 by the German astronomer Caroline Herschel, who described it as a beautiful cluster of pretty compressed stars near 1/2 degree in diameter”.

NGC 2360 is situated close to the celestial equator and, as such, it is, at least, partly visible from both hemispheres during certain times of the year.

description: Also listed as Caldwell 64, this young cluster located in the constellation Canis Major contains several hundred stars. The brightest star is Tau Canis Majoris, a supergiant 50 times more massive than our Sun.
name: Tau Canis Majoris Cluster
trivia: - The cluster was formed about 8 million years ago, when the first line of the human species appeared on Earth (first primates showing human characteristics).

description: Also called the Peanut Nebula, NGC 2371 is a planetary nebula with 3 main structural features: two diametrically opposite lobes and a central peanut-like enveloppe. The dying star responsible for this chaotic event has now reached the extremely hot surface temperature of approximately 100,000 degrees. This high temperature produces a highly energetic UV radiation that heats up the neighboring gas and causes it to glow in the visible light domain. In NGC 2371’s case, the emitted blue light indicates a rich concentration of oxygen.
name: Gemini Nebula
trivia: - Although the famed astronomer W. Herschel discovered NGC 2371 back in 1785, this deep sky object was accurately identified as a planetary nebula only later, in 1917, by astronomer Francis Pease.

description: The Eskimo Nebula is a bipolar planetary nebula with a double shell. It is located in the constellation Gemini.
name: Eskimo Nebula
trivia: - The Eskimo Nebula is known for the exceptionally high rate of expansion of its internal shell, about 55 miles/s, and the existence of rapid bipolar flow with a radial velocity approaching 125 miles/s. The distance from Earth to NGC 2392 is approximately 3,750 light-years.

description: NGC 2403 is a spiral galaxy located 11 million light-years away from the Milky Way, in the constellation Camelopardalis, the Giraffe. The northern spiral arm is home to a giant star-forming region, NGC 2404, an open star cluster associated with an emission nebula. Bright stars, part of our own Milky Way, are visible in the foreground.
name: NGC 2403
trivia:
- NGC 2403 is similar in shape and size to M33, the Triangulum galaxy.
- In 2004, two supernovae were observed in this galaxy, designated as SN 1954J and SN 2004DJ. These supernovae were 16 times brighter than the average.

description:
Located in the Lynx constellation, the star cluster NGC 2419 is estimated to be 10 million years old. It is one of the most distant globular clusters of the Milky Way in our solar system, which explains a lower luminosity than other better-known clusters such as Omega Centauri, located at 160,000 A.L.

The position of the 3 stars HD 60771, double star HD 60694 and TYC 2958-870-1, near the globular cluster, reminds the shape of the Big Dipper's handle.
name: Intergalactic Wanderer
trivia:
- NGC 2419 is also called The Intergalactic Wanderer because it was once mistakenly believed that the object was not orbiting the galaxy. Scientists today believe that its movement is linked to our galaxy by gravity. 
 
Based on its distance (300,000 A.L. from Earth), it takes NGC 2419 about 3 billion years to complete an orbit around the Milky Way.

description: NGC 246, also known as Caldwell 56 or the Skull Nebula, is a planetary nebula in the Cetus Constellation. It formed 6,600 years ago when the outer layers of a star, with an initial mass of 4.3 solar masses, were ejected. The nebula grows at a speed of about 35km/s, although its rate of expansion slows as it comes into contact with the interstellar medium. This shell of oxygen and hydrogen-rich material has already reached 2.1 light-years in size.
name: Skull Nebula
trivia: The centre of the nebula actually contains a three star system! There is a 0.84 solar mass white dwarf star which ejected the nebula, a 0.85 solar mass orange dwarf star (known as K V) and a 0.1 solar mass red dwarf star (known as M V).

description: NGC 2467 is an emission nebula associated with a star cluster, or rather a superposition of several groups of stars located on the same line of sight, at different distances. We observe in this stellar nursery young stars at different stages of formation, young stars whose birth nebula has already dispersed, stars detaching from their cocoon of birth gas or stars that have just been formed.
name: Skull and Crossbones Nebula
trivia: - The ESO (European Southern Observatory) has given NGC 2467 the nickname of The Pirate of the Southern Skies while others compare it to a mandrill, a cousin of the baboon, due to its vivid colors.

description: NCC 247, or Caldwell 62, is an intermediate spiral galaxy in the Cetus Constellation. It is 70,000 light-years across and has a mass equivalent to 75 billion Suns. It belongs to the Sculptor group of galaxies, dominated by the larger NGC 253 and NGC 300 galaxies. Caldwell 62 has a gap in one of its arms and a recent study revealed that no stars have formed in this region over the last billion years, in contrast to those outside the hole. The gas in this region may have been removed by a gravitational interaction with another galaxy, preventing the birth of new stars.
name: NGC 247
trivia: In 2011, astronomers showed that NGC 247 was in fact 1 million light-years closer to us than previously thought. Using ESO instruments, researchers showed that Cepheid Variables, used to calculate distances, were hidden by more dust than expected. This new analysis indicates that NGC 247 is, in fact, 11 million light years away.

description:
The Electric Guitar Cluster, also known as the Termite Hole Cluster, Caldwell 71, or NGC 2477, is an open cluster in the Puppis constellation. At one billion years old, the cluster still contains 2,699 members according to the latest Gaia satellite data. It is therefore one of the most star-rich open clusters in the southern sky. In the sky, the cluster will appear slightly smaller in size than the full moon.
The cluster is moving away from us at 7.3 km/s, in other words, at over 26,000 km/h or the equivalent of a round trip from New York to Cape Town in one hour.
name: Electric Guitar Cluster
trivia:
When the stars in the cluster were forming, a supercontinent, Rodinia, had just assembled on Earth. It broke up into 8 pieces 250 million years later.

In May 2022, Nirvana frontman Kurt Cobain's 1969 Fender Mustang sold for $4.6 million and became the most expensive electric guitar in history and the 2nd most expensive guitar in any category behind the Martin 1959 D-18E used by the same Kurt Cobain during the 1994 MTV Unplugged concert, which sold for $6 million.

description: NGC 2506, also known as Caldwell 54, is an open cluster in the Monoceros constellation. Based on data from the Gaia mission, 1487 stars belong to this cluster. The stars are estimated to be 1.6 billion years old. In the cluster, an estimated 40% of the stars are not alone but in fact, belong to a binary system. The stars live in pairs. As in the case of many clusters, we find stars called blue stragglers. In the case of NGC 2506, there are 14 stars hotter and more massive than the rest of its members. They appear blue compared to the other stars.
name: NGC 2506
trivia:
One of the stars in the NGC 2506-G31 cluster resembles our Sun. It will be used to calibrate JWST observatory instruments.

When the stars in the cluster formed, and based on the estimated age of fossils discovered in Chitrakoot, India, the earliest-known algae using photosynthesis were developing on Earth.

description: NGC 2516, also known as the Caldwell 96 or the Sprinter Cluster, is an open star cluster in the Carina Constellation. According to research, this cluster contains at least 800 stars that are roughly 175 million years old. The stars present have masses reaching double that of the Sun and surface temperatures rising to 10,000°C. Some of them also have a luminosity of up to twenty times that of the Sun. The cluster looks like the Pleiades, with a comparable number of stars of similar age. That said, it is more distant and less easy to observe.
name: Sprinter Cluster
trivia:
- The cluster was used in the calibration and focusing stage for the Gaia satellite.
- In a 2021 study, researchers showed that a halo 1,630 light years away from the cluster appears to contain stars of similar age and chemical composition, suggesting a shared past history.

description: NGC 253 is a starburst galaxy, experiencing extreme star formation, in the constellation of Sculptor. The Sculptor Galaxy is one of the brightest galaxies in the sky, and is easily observable with any kind of instrument.
name: Sculptor Galaxy
trivia:
- It's sometimes called the Silver Coin or Silver Dollar Galaxy.

- It's one of the best sights in the night sky after the Andromeda galaxy.

description: NGC 2683 is a spiral galaxy in the Lynx constellation. The galaxy is moving away from us at a speed of 410 km/s. The galaxy contains about 300 globular clusters, twice the known number found in the Milky Way. It is surrounded by at least 4 satellite galaxies, the largest of which is 12,000 light-years in diameter or ⅔ the size of the Small Magellanic Cloud. The near edge-on galaxy is considerably reddened by the dust and cold gas clouds it contains.
name: NGC 2683
trivia: The galaxy seems to form few stars. Studies have shown that there aren’t many molecular clouds in the galaxy. This means there is no reserve of matter to form new stars.

description: The Pencil Nebula is a small part of the Vela Supernova Remnant, located near the Vela Pulsar in the constellation Vela. Its elongated appearance seemed made of braided filaments which are actually long ripples in a cosmic sheet of glowing gas seen almost edge-on. Its source supernova exploded approximately 12,000 years ago, creating a shock wave which now plows through space at over 500,000 kilometers per hour, which accounts for the unusual shape of the nebula.
name: Pencil Nebula
trivia: - The Pencil nebula was discovered by British astronomer John Herschel at the Cape of Good Hope who described it as an extraordinary long narrow ray of excessively feeble light.

description: NGC 2775 is a spiral galaxy located in the constellation Cancer, approximately 67 million light-years away from Earth. It is also known as Caldwell 48. With a diameter of about 90,000 light-years, it is estimated to have a mass of around 100 billion times that of the Sun.
name: Caldwell 48
trivia: NGC 2775 is also notable for its interaction with a nearby dwarf galaxy, which has caused a tidal tail to form in its outer regions. This tidal tail is a long stream of gas and stars that has been pulled away from the main body of the galaxy by the gravitational forces of the nearby companion.

description: NGC 2808 is a globular cluster located in the constellation Carina. It is 12.5 billion years old and can be observed from the southern hemisphere. NGC 2808 is one of the most massive star clusters in the Milky Way, and contains more than a million stars.
name: NGC 2808
trivia: - NGC 2808 is believed to have originated from the Sausage Galaxy, a dwarf galaxy that was consumed by our Milky Way and gave us at least 8 globular clusters.

description:
NGC 281 is an emission nebula located in the Milky Way’s Perseus spiral arm.
The Pacman nebula got its name because it looks like a famous video game character when seen in wide field. The nebula has a young star cluster, IC 1590, within its star-forming region, which lights up the gases around it.
name: Pacman Nebula
trivia:
- It resembles a video game character.

- Star cluster IC 1590 within the gases.

description: Located in the Southern constellation of Sculptor, NGC 288 is a low-concentration globular cluster found by astronomer Willian Herschel in 1785. With a pair of binoculars, it can be observed in the same field as the popular Sculptor galaxy (NGC 253). NGC 288 is estimated to be 10 billion years old and located about 30,000 light-years from Earth.
name: NGC 288
trivia: A study released in 2016 by Italian astronomers estimated the presence of dark matter within the NGC 288 cluster. Therefore, 75% of its entire mass would be caused by this enigmatic matter we cannot detect directly but which explains the cluster’s current state of dynamics and evolution. The visible mass was derived from Hubble Space Telescope images and from ground-based ESO’s La Silla 2.2 meter telescope. The missing mass, the so-called dark matter, was estimated using light spectra of hundreds of stars thanks to the multi-object spectrograph FLAMES at the ESO’s Very Large Telescope. Once converted into relative velocities between the stars, these spectra enable us to see that dynamical motions of the cluster cannot only be caused by the mass of the individual stars but by an “invisible” missing mass we call dark matter.

description: NGC 2903 is a barred spiral galaxy located about 25 million light-years away in the constellation Leo. It was discovered in 1784 by William Herschel.
name: NGC 2903
trivia: - The NASA / IPAC Extragalactic database classifies this galaxy as a spiral galaxy. Scientists realized that this was a mistake after a photo of the Hubble Space Telescope showed that the galaxy is actually barred.

description: Easily visible to the naked eye, the Small Magellanic Cloud, also known as NGC 292, is a dwarf galaxy in the Tucana constellation. It is the 4th closest extragalactic object to us at only 200,000 light-years away from our galaxy. This proximity means that this satellite galaxy, which was probably once a spiral galaxy, was deformed by interactions with the Milky Way to become irregular. We currently estimate that the SMC contains a few hundred million stars and weighs 7 billion solar masses. There is also a bridge of gas that connects it to the Large Magellanic Cloud, which is evidence of interaction between the two galaxies as well. This is a star-forming region.
name: Small Magellanic Cloud
trivia:
- Although long known to the indigenous peoples of the southern hemisphere and Spanish and Portuguese explorers, this hazy patch, visible to the naked eye, is the namesake of the explorer Magellan who observed the galaxies during his world tour.

- While studying Cepheid variable stars in the Small Magellanic Cloud, Henrietta Leavitt discovered the relationship between a Cepheid star’s variation period and its luminosity. The Discovery of this relationship established a reliable method of measuring the distance of galaxies near us.

description: NGC 2997 is a spiral galaxy belonging to a little-known constellation of the Southern sky whose name is Antlia. We owe this constellation to French astronomer Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille who named it in the 1750’s when he travelled to the Southern Hemisphere. 40 years later, the illustrious British astronomer William Herschel observed NGC 2997 galaxy for the first time using his 17” telescope. NGC 2997 is a superb galaxy with white and blue spiral arms. It is located at 12 Megaparsec and its mass is estimated to 210 billion solar masses, about two times less than the Andromeda galaxy.
name: NGC 2997
trivia:
NGC 2997 is the greatest spiral member of the group LGG 180 which consists of 8 other galaxies like IC 2507. This association was first reported by astronomer A.M Garcia in 1993.
NGC 2997 is neutral-hydrogen-rich. This chemical element, known by specialists as ‘HI’ is a cold gas that plays a key-role in the formation of nebulae within galaxies and so stars but is barely detectable. NGC 2997 is a prime target for astronomers since it shares similarities in structure and composition with M31 due to these hydrogen-rich accretion regions.

description: NGC 300, also known as Caldwell 70, is a spiral galaxy in the Sculptor constellation. It is also called the Southern Pinwheel Galaxy because it resembles M101. With a diameter of 40,000 light-years, it is smaller than our galaxy. In the sky, its size represents ⅔ of the full Moon. As for mass, it is estimated to be 30 billion times that of the Sun. This galaxy does not have a central bulge - the very bright area densely populated with stars that we find in our galaxy.
name: Southern Pinwheel Galaxy
trivia: In 2010, an extremely luminous source appeared in the galaxy suggesting the presence of a supernova. Monitoring over time revealed that what actually occurred was a violent eruption on the surface of a massive star of the Luminous Blue Variable type and that this star is still present.

description:
NGC 3109 is an irregular dwarf galaxy located in the Hydra constellation - the widest spread constellation of our sky. This low surface brightness and details-poor galaxy is the primary member of a larger association group of galaxies discovered in 2006 and whose members are: Antlia, Sextans A and Sextans B. One suggests this galactic group would orbit the Milky Way and would be part of the local group.
A special property of NGC 3109 is its relative motion to our galaxy: it is moving outwards at a speed of 403 km/s. In addition to be dizzying, this figure is 105 km/s higher than what astronomers’ computations suggest. Some theories assume this galaxy would have gained such excess of speed while approaching the center of the Milky Way. NGC 3109 is thus part of a broad category of galaxies called “backsplashers” which have already crossed or passed by the center of mass of a galactic cluster or a galaxy.
name: NGC 3109
trivia: In 2015, observations carried out with the American telescope CTIO and its 570 megapixels camera revealed the presence of a new galaxy in gravitational interaction with NGC 3109. Named Antlia B, it is a dwarf type galaxy that hides a fascinating stellar population: some stars are as old as 10 billion years whereas others are as young as 400 million years! Antlia B and its big sister Antlia are a couple of galaxies containing a rich amount of neutral hydrogen. Astronomers are not entirely certain where this high concentration comes from, especially when the rest of the Milky Way’s satellite galaxies are deprived of it. The close environment of NGC 3109 still raises questions to the astronomy community.

description: NGC 3114 is an open cluster in the Carina constellation. The roughly 130-million-year-old stars in this cluster are 2,250 light-years away from the Earth. The study of this region to determine which stars are part of the cluster is complicated by the presence of many field stars. It is currently estimated that the cluster contains at least 1,000 stars. In this relatively young cluster, Sun-like stars are at the very beginning of their several billion years of life while stars with a mass of more than 20 times that of the Sun have already disappeared.
name: NGC 3114
trivia: When the stars in the cluster were formed, Earth was populated by such dinosaurs as Brachiosaurus; at 26 meters long, 12 meters high, and weighing in at 50 tons, they are among the largest known.

description:
The Spindle galaxy is a very particular galaxy in the Sextant constellation. Located 31 million light-years away, its physical properties situate it halfway between a spiral galaxy and an elliptical galaxy. Emitting a very diffuse and evenly distributed light, NGC 3115 presents very little detail. It remains nevertheless a fascinating object for astronomers as it contains: a central disc-shaped nucleus, a fine ring structure with aborted spiral arms as well as a large population of globular clusters. It is the closest galaxy to the solar system according to these particular criteria.
In 1992, two American astronomers discovered a supermassive black hole using NASA's Chandra X-ray telescope. Its mass is estimated at 2 billion times that of the Sun!
name: Spindle Galaxy
trivia: In 2020, other research work was done to reveal the true nature of NGC 3115 and why it evolved into such a strange structure. Based on archived data from the Keck telescope in Hawaii, the study suggests this galaxy was initially a spiral, before it encountered a low-mass neighbor galaxy about 9 billion years ago. This collision resulted in the ellipse-like structure we see today and could have triggered the formation of multiple globular clusters. Currently, no less than 150 such clusters were observed in NGC 3115!

description:
Like the Ring nebula in the Northern Hemisphere, the Southern Ring Nebula is a marvelous planetary nebula dedicated to southern observers and situated in the Vela constellation. Its name reflects its specific ellipsoid structure.
The star responsible for this ejection of hot gas is not the one we can easily spot at the center of the nebula in pictures made with amateur telescopes. The genuine star, a white dwarf whose surface temperature is averaging 100,000 degrees, is exclusively visible with professional telescopes because of its low brightness and proximity to its neighbor. Moreover, both stars do not appear close due to a line-of-sight effect: they are really close to each other since they are making a binary star system.
name: Southern Ring Nebula
trivia:
A picture of this nebula enables us to emphasize the dramatic variations in colors - and so in temperature - within its shell: the internal region, closer to the boiling white dwarf, appears in blue unlike its external region that appears in red since it is further away and so colder than its core.
The distance to this nebula has long been approximative, ranging from 1,760 to 4,000 light-years! In 2018, some results based on a high-precision astrometric map made by Gaia satellite plummeted the uncertainty of the measurements to a distance between 2,687 and 2,948 light-years; As usual, the technical progress keeps benefiting astronomy!

description: NGC 3190 is a spiral galaxy in the Leo constellation. It is surrounded by the NGC 3185, NGC 3187, and NGC 3193 galaxies. These four galaxies form the Leo Quartet, also known as Hickson 44. These galaxies are about 80 million light-years away from us. NGC 3190 hosts a supermassive black hole within its core that weighs 126 million solar masses, which is about 30 times more massive than the Milky Way. The near edge-on galaxy appears yellow because the blue light emitted by the young stars is absorbed by the dust.
name: Leo Quartet
trivia:
