NGC 663, also known as Caldwell 10, is an open cluster in the Cassiopeia constellation. The Gaia Mission identified 468 stars in this cluster. The hottest of them has a surface temperature of almost 13,000 degrees, which is more than twice the temperature of the Sun's surface and 13 times that required to melt gold. And the coldest one it was possible to measure has a temperature equal to that of the Sun. These stars and their companions formed 30 million years ago. 
The cluster also contains at least 24 Be-type stars. A distinguishing feature of these stars is that they spin very quickly on themselves, faster than 300 km/s, and are consequently heavily flattened.
name: NGC 663
trivia: When the stars formed, the common ancestor of whales produced toothed whales (orcas) and baleen whales (humpbacks).

description: NGC 6624 is a 7th-magnitude globular cluster located in the teapot-shaped asterism of the constellation Sagittarius (The Archer), discovered by William Herschel in 1784. It lies less than two full Moon widths to the lower-left for Northern Hemisphere observers (upper-right south of the equator) of the naked-eye star Delta Sagittarii. Astronomers believe that NGC 6624 is about 25,800 light-years from Earth, where its apparent size of 8.8' translates to an actual diameter of 66 light-years.
name: NGC 6624
trivia: The stars of NGC 6624 are about 12 billion years old.

description: NGC 6633, also called the Captain Hook Cluster, is an open cluster in the Ophiuchus constellation. In the sky, it is a large cluster that is nearly the size of the full Moon. The latest studies conducted with Gaia data show that the cluster contains at least 100 stars and that it is about 700 million years old. While Sun-like stars are at less than 10% of their life, stars larger than five solar masses are already dead.
name: Captain Hook Cluster
trivia: For the English, the cluster is also called Tweedledum and its twin brother, Tweedledee, is the open cluster IC 4756. We find these two characters in particular in the universe of Alice in Wonderland.

description:
NGC 6709, also known as The Flying Unicorn Cluster, is an open cluster in the Aquila constellation. It is around 150 million years old, about the same as the Pleiades. It contains 305 stars according to the last census performed by the Gaia Mission, in other words, ten times less than the Pleiades cluster. The hottest stars in the cluster have surface temperatures of 14,000 degrees.

The stars in the cluster are moving towards us at a speed of 7.8 km/s or 28,000 km/h. This is ten times faster than the cruising speed of the JWST when it was traveling to its observation mission position.
name: Flying Unicorn Cluster
trivia: On November 13, 1984, the comet hunter, David H. Levy, discovered his first Levy-Rudenko comet (1984t) at less than 1° from the cluster.

description:
NGC 6712 is a small globular cluster situated in the fifth smallest constellation: Scutum. Like a lot of other globular clusters within this area of the sky, it also belongs to the galactic bulge.
Astrophysicists have recently discovered that NGC 6712 would have, at multiple times, been in interaction with the Milky Way’s bulge leading to a dispersion of its stellar members on its course. Because of these recurrent encounters, some stars would have been disseminated in the orbital plane of the galaxy and would head toward its core.
name: NGC 6712
trivia: A 2019 study led with two telescopes from the Canary Islands and India enabled scientists to detect more than 60,000 stars nearby the NGC 6712 globular cluster. Based on astrometric data obtained with Gaia, they could confirm that only 1,500 of them would be part of the cluster. Such a low proportion of star members compared to what was initially observed is due to the complexity of observing a region in the vicinity of the galactic bulge: the star density is so high it reduces the chances to detect isolated stars or stars that are deprived of any light contamination caused by others.

description: NGC 6723, also known as the Chandelier Cluster, is a globular cluster in the Sagittarius constellation. In the Milky Way, the cluster is located in the galactic bulge less than 3,300 light-years from the center of the Galaxy, or eight times closer than we are to the galactic center. It is 12.5 billion years old. The mass of all the stars is estimated to be 172,000 times that of the Sun. It basically consists of old, low-mass stars, that is, with masses within the range of the Sun or even lower. Only 36% of the stars it contains formed during the first star-burst event, the rest formed later, during a second star-forming event.
name: Chandelier Cluster
trivia: If we were to say that the Sun weighs 1 kg, then the mass of the cluster would be slightly more than that of a blue whale.

description:
NGC 6726 is a reflection nebula in the Corona Australis constellation. This gigantic cloud of gas and fine dust reflects the blue light from the stars in the nearby cluster on its surface. In the latter, only two stars are observable in visible light, R Coronae Australis (R CrA) and T Coronae Australis (T CrA). The 12 other stars in the cluster are buried in the gas cloud and are only visible because of their infrared signature. We should also note the presence of reflection nebula NGC 6729. Dust and gas surrounding R CrA reflects a portion of the light emitted by the star.
R CrA is in fact a binary system that consists of a star with a mass of 3.5 solar masses and a companion with a mass of 2.3 solar masses. The stars orbit each other in 45 years. The system is estimated to be 1 million years old.
name: NGC 6726
trivia:
- There are as many known stars in the cluster as the maximum number of clubs in a golf bag.

- There are as many stars in the cluster as there are toes on a guinea pig’s paws.

- R CrA is in fact a binary system that consists of a star with a mass of 3.5 solar masses and a companion with a mass of 0.5 solar masses. The stars orbit each other in 45 years. The system is estimated to be 1 million years old.

description: Magnitude 8.3 spiral galaxy NGC 6744, also known as Caldwell 101, is the brightest example in the southern constellation Pavo (The Peacock). Scottish astronomer James Dunlop discovered it in 1826. About 30 million light-years from Earth, astronomers believe it closely resembles how our Milky Way would look from afar. However, NGC 6744's apparent size of 20' implies a diameter of about 175,000 light-years, making it two-thirds larger than our Milky Way. Its northern spiral arm exhibits gravitational distortion from its dwarf companion, NGC 6744A, which lies 10' to the northwest.
name: Caldwell 101
trivia:
NGC 6744 is a member of the Virgo Supercluster, also known as the Local Supercluster, which consists of approximately 10,000 galaxies, including the Milky Way and Andromeda galaxies.
The galaxy hosted supernova SN 2005at discovered on 15 March 2005.

description: NGC 6752, popularly known as the Great Peacock Cluster or Caldwell 93, is a bright globular cluster discovered by Scottish astronomer James Dunlop in 1826. It lies in the Southern Hemisphere constellation Pavo (The Peacock), hence its nickname. Glowing at magnitude 5.4, NGC 6752 borders on naked-eye visibility and contains hundreds of thousands of stars around 11.78 billion years old. Astronomers believe that NGC 6752 is about 13,000 light-years from Earth, where its 20' apparent size (two-thirds of the full Moon's diameter) suggests an actual diameter of 75 light-years.
name: Caldwell 93
trivia: NGC 6752 ranks as the fourth-brightest globular cluster visible from Earth.

description: NGC 6760 is a 9th-magnitude globular cluster in the constellation Aquila (The Eagle) discovered by English astronomer John Hind in 1845. It lies about 24,100 light-years from Earth, so its apparent size of 9.6' corresponds to an actual diameter of 67 light-years. NGC 6760 lies almost on the celestial equator; hence it is equally observable from the Northern and Southern Hemispheres.
name: NGC 6760
trivia: The mass of NGC 6760 is 357,000 times that of the Sun.

description: NGC 6781 is a planetary nebula, also known as “Ghost of the Moon” or “Snowball”, located in the Aquila constellation. About 9,400 years ago, a star between 2.25 and 3 times the mass of the Sun ejected a huge amount of gas (20% of the star's mass) into the interstellar medium. The rest of the star, in the center of the nebula, has a luminosity 100 times greater than that of the Sun and a surface temperature estimated at 100,000°C, which is 35 times greater than the boiling point of iron. This stellar residue heats up the barrel-shaped nebula and the various excited chemical components glow in different colors.
name: Ghost of the Moon
trivia:
In 2016, more than 2,000 planetary nebulas were identified in the Milky Way - as many as the last representatives of the Ganges River Gharial, the endangered Asian crocodile species.
When the planetary nebula formed 9,400 years ago, the Earth faced rising sea levels and the British Isles separated from Europe.

description: NGC 6791 is a 9th-magnitude open cluster in the constellation Lyra (The Lyre) discovered by German astronomer Friedrich Winnecke in 1853. It lies about a span of a fist at arm's length east of Vega, the fifth brightest star in the night sky. NGC 6791 is a population-rich open cluster and one of the oldest known at 8 billion years. It lies about 13,000 light-years from Earth, where its apparent size of 10' suggests an actual diameter of around 38 light-years. In April 2009, NGC 6791 was one of the first objects photographed by the Kepler Mission spacecraft designed to discover extrasolar planets.
name: NGC 6791
trivia: The most ancient stars in NGC 6791 are 8 billion years old.

description: Barnard's Galaxy, also known as NGC 6822 or IC 4895, is an irregular galaxy in the Sagittarius constellation. Located less than 2 million light-years away, it is one of the closest galaxies to the Milky Way. This small galaxy, 7,000 light-years in diameter, only contains about ten or so million stars, most of which are still young, and the presence of massive stars gives the galaxy its bluish color. There are as many stars in this galaxy as there were inhabitants in the Mayan empire.
name: Barnard's Galaxy
trivia: In 1925, the astronomer Edwin Hubble identified 15 variable stars, of which 11 were of the Cepheid type, in NGC 6822. Using the relationship between the luminosity of these stars and their pulsation period, he determined a distance of 698,000 light-years. This result put an end to the Great Debate on the nature of spiral nebulas, which are now identified as galaxies and not objects of our Milky Way. This result opened the door to extragalactic astronomy.

description: NGC 6820 and NGC 6823 are not very popular targets, mostly because they are often outshone by the nearby Dumbbell Nebula (Messier 27). NGC 6823 is a pretty small reflection nebula that is located very close to the open cluster NGC 6820. The two are usually mentioned in pairs as they are almost always photographed together.
name: NGC 6823
trivia: - By getting a nice picture of the nebula and zooming in a little, we can see beautiful blue stars that form pillars of gas. These stars are very young and have only been shining for the past 2 million years. The formed gas pillars will in turn make new stars themselves. There is some similarities with the very famous Pillars of Creation in the Eagle Nebula.

description: NGC 6826 is a small planetary nebula found in the constellation Cygnus, the Swan. It is part of a type of planetary nebulae called the Blink nebulae ; depending on how they are observed, either through direct visual observation or photographic, they appear to be blinking.
name: Blinking Nebula
trivia: - The nebula is visible to the naked eye but can be lost within the stars around her, making her difficult to spot though not impossible. To locate her, use the Theta Cygni star, near lota, as a guide. It is more diffuse than a star and does not shine on its own.

description: NGC 6872, also known as the Condor Galaxy, is an unusually shaped 11th-magnitude spiral in the far southern constellation Pavo (The Peacock) discovered by English polymath John Herschel in 1835. Its wide-spread wings resulted from gravitational interactions with smaller galaxy IC 4970 to the north about 130 million years ago. Some 700,000 light-years from tip to tip, or seven times the diameter of the Milky Way, NGC 6872 is the largest known spiral galaxy. However, the Condor Galaxy is about 400,000 light-years across at visual wavelengths, so it appears 6.5' wide from Earth at a distance of 212 million light-years.
name: Condor Galaxy
trivia: Use Singularity to capture the Condor Galaxy and NGC 6876, an 11th-magnitude elliptical 9' to its southeast, and more galaxies in this field.

description:
The Crescent Nebula is an emission nebula located in the constellation of the swan: Cygnus, about 5,000 light-years away. 
Its structure and colors come from Wolf-Rayet 136, a hot star located in the center of the nebula ejecting its matter in the form of powerful stellar winds.
name: Crescent Nebula
trivia:
- This dense cosmic bubble, produced by the collision of different stellar winds, continues to expand at a speed of 50 miles per second. 
 
- Due to its shape, it is also sometimes called the Euro Sign Nebula.

description: The Little Ring or Diamond Ring Nebula, also known as NGC 6894, is a planetary nebula in the Cygnus constellation. Created from the matter expelled by a solar-type star at the end of its life, the nebula is expanding at a speed of 43 km/s. The mass of the nebula is estimated at about 0.2 solar masses. The gas of the nebula is heated by the intense light emitted by the residual white dwarf star at the center that shines with a luminosity of 300 suns.
name: Little Ring Nebula
trivia: The central star of the planetary nebula ionizes the surrounding interstellar medium. Beyond the nebula, researchers noted the unique presence of emission gas stripes. These are thought to be caused by the galactic magnetic field, which forces the gas to align along field lines.

description: NGC 6905, referred to as the Blue Flash nebula, is a small planetary nebula housed in the constellation Delphinus, the Dolphin. It is identified by its oblong form and pointed extremities which are more difficult to observe.
name: Blue Flash Nebula
trivia: - Can you find the white dwarf at its center? It is estimated that the surface of this star reaches 150 000 degrees.

description:
NGC 6910 is a small open cluster that sits only a half-degree northeast of Sadr (Gamma Cygni), the bright central star in the prominent northern constellation Cygnus, the swan.
Discovered in 1828 by noted English astronomer John Herschel, this sparkly elongated patch of stars shines with an overall apparent magnitude of 7.4, making it even visible through binoculars. While the cluster’s brightest member is a dazzling, blue supergiant star, a telescope is needed to really bring into view the many fainter stellar members, many of them sparkling in distinct yellow and orange hues making the color contrasts quite eye-catching.
Gaze carefully at the overall shape of NGC 6910 and its core of brightest 35 member stars appear together as a crooked Y-shaped asterism.
Since NGC 6910 appears so close to the bright star Sadr, observers will immediately notice that it appears embedded within the large, ghost-like nebulosity.
name: NGC 6910
trivia: Astronomers believe that while NGC 6910 is less than 6 light years wide, it actually represents the core cluster of a much larger group of stars stretching out into a stellar stream more than 175 light years long, known as the Cygnus OB9.

description: NGC 6914 is a complex of emission, reflection, and absorption nebulae in the Cygnus constellation, near the star Sadr. This region of our galaxy, which extends over 1/2 degree in our sky, is actually an area that spans 50 or so light-years. The massive, hot, young stars of the Cygnus OB2 association, which are behind this gas cloud, heat the gas. Hydrogen, the main constituent of the cloud, will emit in the red and help us understand the cloud’s structure. The young cluster is composed of about 50 massive stars and has an estimated mass of 30,000 solar masses.
name: NGC 6914
trivia: Although the stars in the star association share a common formation region, they are currently no longer bound by gravity and therefore do not form an open cluster. Although the stars in the association are young and it is still a star-forming region, some are evolved and close to the end of their life. There are WR-type stars and LBV-type stars that radiate intensely and expel large amounts of material.

description: NGC 6934, also known as Caldwell 47, is a globular cluster in the Delphinus constellation. 50,000 light-years away from Earth, it is situated in the outer reaches of our galaxy. With 250,000 stars, the cluster has as many members as there were inhabitants of New York City in the 1830s. The total mass of this cluster is estimated to be 300,000 times that of the Sun. At 11 billion years old, it is not one of the oldest clusters in the Milky Way, some of which attain 13 billion years.
name: NGC 6934
trivia:
- The Delphinus constellation to which the cluster belongs is one of the 48 constellations listed by Ptolemy in the 2nd century. For Arab astronomers, it is the camel constellation.

- The Delphinus constellation, in which NGC 6934 is located, has two main stars: α (Alpha) Delphini and β (Beta) Delphini. They are also known as Sualocin and Rotanev. These are the first and last names of astronomer Giuseppe Piazzi’s assistant Nicolaus Venator, written backwards.

description: NGC 6946 is a face-on spiral galaxy, located between the Cepheus constellation and Cygnus the Swan. It finds its nickname in the multiple supernovae (explosion of a star) which have been observed in the galaxy, a rate 10 times higher than that of the Milky Way (1 supernova event in average observed in a century).
name: Fireworks Galaxy
trivia:
- 10 supernovae have been observed since 1917, the last being in 2017.

- The galaxy is 3 times smaller and has 2 times fewer stars than our galaxy, the Milky Way.

description: NGC 6948 is a spiral galaxy located in the Indus constellation, a constellation visible from the Southern Hemisphere. A very distant galaxy, it is located 149 million light-years from Earth, and presents a low magnitude. We can observe it by its edge and notice a prominent central bulb.
name: NGC 6948
trivia: - By comparison, the Andromeda spiral galaxy is located 2.5 million light-years away. The Sombrero galaxy, a galaxy also seen from its edge, is 31 million light-years from Earth.

description: The Veil nebula, also often called the Witch’s Broom nebula or Bridal Veil nebula, is a beautiful diffuse nebula that is actually a cloud of heated and ionized gas divided into three parts. The Western Veil (NGC 6960) is the most popular one, followed by the Eastern Veil (NGC 6992), and finally Pickering’s Triangle (NGC 6979).
name: Veil Nebula (NGC6960)
trivia: - The Veil nebula is a large supernova remnant that constitutes the Cygnus Loop.

description: The Veil nebula, also often called the Witch’s Broom nebula or Bridal Veil nebula, is a beautiful diffuse nebula that is actually a cloud of heated and ionized gas divided into three parts. The Western Veil (NGC 6960) is the most popular one, followed by the Eastern Veil (NGC 6992), and finally Pickering’s Triangle (NGC 6979).
name: Veil Nebula (NGC6992)
trivia: - The Veil nebula is a large supernova remnant that constitutes the Cygnus Loop.

description: The North America nebula is huge, more than four times the size of the moon, and got its name because in photographs, looks like the North American continent. Right next to this nebula is the Pelican nebula. Both objects are divided by a wall of dark nebulosity, called the Cygnus Wall.
name: North America Nebula
trivia: - The main bright stars in the gases form the “Little Orion” asterism.

description: NGC 7006, also known as Caldwell 42, is a globular cluster in the Delphinus constellation. It resides in the outer reaches of the Milky Way and is at 5 times the distance between the Sun and the center of the galaxy. Because of its very eccentric orbit, the cluster could have formed outside the Milky Way and been absorbed afterwards. The mass of the stars that compose it is estimated to be 300,000 times that of the Sun, distributed among about 250,000 stars. This amount of stars corresponds to the number of inhabitants in Kyoto in the 1880s. As in the case in other globular clusters, variable stars have been detected in NGC 7006. There are currently 60 stars with a luminosity that can vary between a few hours and a few days.
name: NGC 7006
trivia: Edgar Rice Burroughs, the creator of Tarzan among others, wrote the short story Beyond the Farthest Star in the 1940s in which reference is made to NGC 7006. The planet in his story is located beyond the globular cluster.

description: NGC 7008, also called the Fetus Nebula, is a planetary nebula with a diameter of about 1 light-year, It is located 2,800 light-years away in the constellation of Cygnus.
name: Fetus Nebula
trivia: - It was discovered by William Herschel in 1787 in Slough, England.

description: NGC 7009 is a planetary nebula which, seen from the Earth, strongly resembles the planet Saturn (hence its nickname of Saturn nebula). It can be found close to M72, M73 and the star V Aquarii in the constellation Aquarius.
name: Saturn Nebula
trivia: - The Saturn Nebula was discovered in 1782 by William Herschel. Although several planetary nebulae were discovered in previous years, this was the first one that was correctly identified as a planetary nebula. William Herschel also proposed the term planetary nebula after this discovery, reminding him of the planet Uranus he discovered earlier.

description: Surrounded by huge clouds of interstellar dust, the Iris nebula is a beautiful, blue reflection nebula in the constellation of Cepheus. NGC 7023 has a bright young star in its center, and the gases gradually darken as it is surrounded by clouds of interstellar dust.
name: Iris Nebula
trivia: - The Iris nebula’s blue gas petals are about six light-years across.

description:
NGC 7038 is a beautiful 11th-magnitude intermediate spiral galaxy in the southern constellation Indus (The Indian) discovered by English polymath John Herschel in 1834. It lies about 220 million light-years from Earth, so its apparent size of 3.2' implies an actual diameter of around 205,000 light-years.
Hence it's about twice the size of our Milky Way galaxy. NGC 7038 has produced three supernovae seen in 1983, 2010 and 2018, so be sure to check your Singularity images for any 'new' stars!
name: NGC 7038
trivia: NGC 7038 lies near the centre of the so-called Pavo–Indus Supercluster of galaxies.

description: NGC 7129 is a reflection nebula discovered by William Herschel on October 18, 1794. Because of its gas, it makes it difficult to observe and study the nearby NGC 7142.
name: Cosmic Rose Nebula
trivia: - Researchers estimate that there are more than 130 very young stars around this nebula. The infrared photographs of the object show a beautiful red nebula shaped like a petal, earning it its nickname cosmic rose.

description: The Helix nebula, also known as the Eye of God, or even the Eye of Sauron, looks like a larger version of the Ring nebula (M57). The Helix nebula contains about 20,000 cometary knots, which are structures linked to the evolution of the nebula. Each knot is usually bigger than the size of our solar system.
name: Helix Nebula
trivia:
- The Helix nebula is the first planetary nebula discovered to contain cometary knots.

- It expands at a speed of 40km/s.

description: Stephan's Quintet is an apparent group of galaxies, first observed by the French astronomer Edward Stephan in 1878. The Stephan Quintet can be found in the constellation Pegasus. The group was cataloged as a cluster of nebulae. At the time, no one could imagine that these were actually entire galaxies made up of billions of stars and located outside our own Milky Way.
name: Stephan's Quintet
trivia:
- Stephan's Quintet is located about 340 million light-years away and has a total of five galaxies: NGC 7317, NGC 7318a, NGC 7318b, NGC 7319, and NGC 7320. The latter is actually an intruder, and is only located 35 million light-years away. It is in fact just in the right spot to make it seem to belong to the group when observed from Earth. As for the others, there is no doubt that they are very close to each other and they each have deformation in their arms, due to the gravitational forces exerted by each one.

- Stephan's Quintet is not visible to the naked eye, and a medium-sized instrument is needed to observe these galaxies.

description: NGC 7331, also known as Caldwell 30, is an unbarred spiral galaxy found about 40 million light-years away in the constellation Pegasus. It is the brightest member of the NGC 7331 Group of galaxies, also called the Deer Lick Group. The core of the galaxy appears to be slightly off-center, with one side of the disk appearing to extend further away from the core than the opposite side.
name: NGC 7331
trivia:
- The galaxy is similar in size and structure to the Milky Way, and is sometimes referred to as the Milky Way's twin, although the Milky Way is now believed to be a barred spiral. 
- The four other members of the NGC 7331 group of galaxies are 10 times further away from Earth than NGC 7331.

description: NGC 7380, faint and very difficult to observe was discovered in 1787 by Caroline Herschel. It lies 7,200 light-years away in the constellation Cepheus. NGC 7380 is pretty large and colorful especially if imaged in narrowband, it has the nickname of Wizard Nebula.
name: Wizard Nebula
trivia: - The Wizard Nebula got its nickname because of the open cluster located in the gases. The stars appear to play with the gas and look like a magical wizard. The measured area of star formation within the nebula has a size larger than the moon.

description: NGC 7424 is a 10th-magnitude barred spiral in the southern constellation Grus (The Crane) discovered by John Herschel in 1834. The galaxy has an apparent size of 9.5', which suggests an actual diameter of 100,000 light-years at its 37 million light-year distance from Earth, making it similar in size to our Milky Way. We see NGC 7424 almost face-on, an aspect that displays its well-defined spiral arms prominently, which is why it is also called the Grand Design Galaxy.
name: NGC 7424
trivia: NGC 7424 hosted magnitude 14.5 supernova 2001ig. It was discovered on 10 December 2001 by Australian Robert Evans, a reverend and amateur astronomer who holds the record for visual discoveries of supernovae.

description: NGC 7479, also known as Caldwell 44 and the Superman Galaxy, is a spiral galaxy in the Pegasus constellation. This galaxy has two long asymmetrical spiral arms. This deformation of the spiral arms is likely due to a past merger with a smaller galaxy. It also has a central bar and this visual aspect makes it look like Superman's S. All parts of the galaxy underwent a major star-forming event less than 100 million years ago. With such recent star formation, the galaxy appears bluish.
name: Superman Galaxy
trivia: Using X-ray and radio observation, NGC 7479 was found to have arms winding in the opposite direction. They would be due to the absorption of a small galaxy in the past.

description:
NGC 752, also known as Caldwell 28, is a very large but loose open cluster situated in the northern Andromeda, the princess constellation.
English astronomer Caroline Herschel discovered this celestial gem back in 1783, and her brother William Herschel cataloged it in 1786. Located 1,400 light-years away from Earth, this expansive cluster is easily observable with binoculars. Under dark skies, it might even become visible to the naked eye as a fuzzy patch of light.
When observed through a telescope, NGC 752 harbours around 60 to 80 stars that stretch across two moon disks in the sky, adding to the celestial spectacle.
name: Caldwell 28
trivia: NGC 752 contains the eclipsing binary called DS Andromeda. As the two stars orbit each other and eclipse each other from our line of sight, its maximum apparent visual magnitude reaches 10.44, and during the main eclipse drops down to 10.93 and then rises in brightness to 10.71 during the secondary eclipse.

description: NGC 7538 is an emission nebula associated with a cluster of forming stars in the Cepheus constellation. The mass of this cluster and gas cloud is estimated to be 400,000 times that of the Sun. It is the closest active star formation factory to us that already has 13 stars with masses greater than 40 Suns. The most massive star in the cloud shines like 100,000 suns and creates jets and streams of matter within the cloud. These jets represent about 130 solar masses. At least 419 young stellar objects, which will soon become stars, were discovered in this nursery. They are less than 2.5 million years old.
name: NGC 7538
trivia: When the young stellar objects were formed, Homo habilis appeared on Earth.

description:
NGC 7635 is pretty unimpressive when observing it through an eyepiece, but it is a wonderful looking target in photographs.
The bubble is very small, but the diffuse gases all around are colorful and expand quite a lot!
name: Bubble Nebula
trivia:
- The Bubble nebula has a radius of 3 to 5 light-years.

- It was created from a huge young central star’s stellar wind.

description: NGC 7662 is a beautiful planetary nebula in the constellation Andromeda. It can be found at 5,600 light-years from Earth and has a magnitude of 9.20. Its color and its shape gave it the nickname of Blue Snowball Nebula.
name: Blue Snowball Nebula
trivia: - Although the nebula itself has a magnitude of 9.20, its central star, which burns at a temperature of 75,000 K and illuminates all the gas around it, has a magnitude of 12.50.

description: Also known as the White Rose, this open cluster located in the Cassiopeia constellation has a diameter of 16'1 (about the diameter of the Moon) and is home to about a thousand stars.
name: Caroline's Rose
trivia: - Cataloged as H VI.30 by the astronomer William Herschel, the cluster is known as « Caroline’s rose » as it was she who discovered the cluster first. The curls formed by the stars look like the swirl formed by rose petals.

description: NGC 7793 is a spiral galaxy in the Sculptor constellation. Its spiral arms are not very structured or visible, which gives the impression it is covered with flakes. The galaxy has a mass of stars estimated at 3 billion Suns. The galaxy contains more than 2,000 young star-forming structures, two-thirds of which are less than 20 million years old. These regions illuminate the different parts of the galaxy blue. It also contains a large amount of gas distributed in clouds, the largest of which measures about 650 light-years for a mass of one million times that of the Sun. New stars will consequently continue to form into the future.
name: NGC 7793
trivia: A binary system containing a 10 solar mass black hole and a 20 solar mass object was detected in the outer reaches of the galaxy. The two objects orbit each other in 68 days. The black hole is ripping and swallowing matter from its companion at a higher rate than expected.

description: NGC 7814 is also known as Caldwell 43 or the Little Sombrero Galaxy due to its resemblance to M104. However, unlike its namesake in Virgo, 11th-magnitude NGC 7814 lies higher in the sky for Northern Hemisphere observers in the constellation Pegasus (The Winged Horse). It's a fine example of a spiral galaxy seen almost edge-on with an equatorial dust lane bisecting the nucleus discovered by German astronomer William Herschel in 1784. The Little Sombrero is about 40 million light-years from Earth, where its 5.5' apparent size suggests an actual diameter of 64,000 light-years.
name: Caldwell 43
trivia: NGC 7814 hosted Type Ia supernova SN 2021rhu in 2021.

description: NGC 864 is a spiral galaxy located in Cetus, the fourth largest constellation in the sky, about 70 million light-years away from the Milky Way. It is in the category of intermediate spiral galaxies; between a regular spiral galaxy and a barred spiral galaxy. Its central bar is fairly weak.
name: NGC 864
trivia: - The NGC 864 galaxy is one of a group of 3 galaxies. The other two galaxies are UGC1670 (Magellanic spiral galaxy) and UGC 1803 9 (barred Magellanic spiral galaxy), it has, therefore, a higher magnitude (14) with weak luminosity.

description: These 3 objects are part of the constellation Aries; a group of 8 galaxies located about 170 million light-years away from the Milky Way. NGC 877 is an intermediate spiral galaxy, the largest of the three. Its closest neighbor is the spiral galaxy NGC 876, seen on its side. Further on, we find NGC 871, a barred spiral galaxy twice as small as its two neighbors.
name: NGC 877 / 876 / 871
trivia:
- NGC 876 and NGC 877 are about the same distance away from earth and together they form a pair of galaxies in gravitational interaction.
- NGC 877 is the brightest galaxy in the group, named LGG 35 scientifically. In this group, one can also find the objects: IC 1791, NGC 871, NGC 876, UGC 1693, UGC 1761, UGC 1773 et UGC 18179.

description: NGC 869 and NGC 884 are two stellar clusters in the constellation of Perseus. Both objects are very similar to each other in size, magnitude, and age. The Double Cluster is located in the constellation of Perseus, but lies just near the “W” shape of Cassiopeia.
name: Double Cluster in Perseus
trivia:
- The Double Cluster in Perseus represents the jewels from the handle of Perseus’ sword.

- It's about twice the size of the Moon.

- Its total mass represents at least 20,000 solar masses.

description: NGC891, also known as Caldwell 23, is a spiral galaxy, although it is only viewed from the edge. It is located in the Andromeda constellation, near the star Almaak. It features a thick dust lane, similar to that found in our galaxy, the Milky Way.
name: NGC 891
trivia:
- The light emitted by the galaxy takes about 30 million light-years (1 ly: ~10 000 billion km or ~6 000 billion miles) to reach us.
- This galaxy has a shape and size similar to our galaxy, the Milky Way, about 100,000 ly. From the outside, our galaxy would look like NGC891, which is why it is of great interest to scientists.

description: NGC 986 is a barred spiral galaxy discovered by James Dunlop in 1828 in the Fornax constellation and located at 56 million light-years away. The faintness of the blue spiral arms of the galaxy are compensated by an interesting bright yellow central bar in which new stars are formed. The amount of light emitted by NGC 986 is equal to about 350 billion times that of the Sun’s; this figure might seem vertiginously high but is not surprising as we know a galaxy can contain a few hundred billion stars.
name: NGC 986
trivia: Barred spiral galaxies are not tremendously rare in the Universe as astronomical surveys indicate they are 1.5 times more common than classical spiral galaxies. NGC 986 is rather rare: in addition to containing a huge amount of ionized hydrogen regions, its central bar is a zone rich in molecular gas, namely carbon monoxide. The central part of NGC 986, 44 light-years long, is therefore the largest molecular gas-rich reservoir ever detected inside a barred spiral. The result was obtained thanks to the radio telescope ASTE: a 10-meter diameter dish located at 4,800 meters altitude in the heart of the Atacama desert. This instrument observes sub-millimetric domains of light for which the interstellar dust is transparent, thus enabling it to probe the internal composition of galaxies and other celestial bodies.

description:
Altair is the brightest star in the Eagle constellation and the 12th brightest star in the night sky.
Along with Deneb in the Cygnus constellation and Vega in the Lyra constellation, they form one of the most well-known asterisms: the Summer Triangle. It is also one of the closest bright stars to the Sun, at just 17 light-years away. Altair is 1.7 times more massive than the Sun and has a higher temperature, resulting in its white-bluish color.
Altair has an extremely rapid rotation speed of 7 hours and 46 minutes (compared to over 25 days for the Sun).
name: Altair
trivia:
Due to its proximity and characteristics, Altair has been a target for the Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence (SETI) research project.
A message was sent toward the star in 1983. It is the first interstellar message that reached its destination (in 2017).

description: The Engagement Ring is an asterism visible by anyone living in the Northern hemisphere. The ring is made up of the few stars visible next to Polaris, and the diamond is represented by the North Star.
name: Polaris
trivia: - In astronomy, a polar star is a star visible to the naked eye lying approximately in alignment with the axis of rotation of a planet, in our case, the Earth.

description:
Polaris (alpha Ursae Minoris) is the brightest star in the constellation of Ursa Minor. It is primarily known for indicating the direction of the geographic north. Indeed, it is located only 0.75 degrees from the celestial North Pole, in line with the Earth's axis of rotation.

With an apparent magnitude of 2, it is not an exceptionally bright star, but it is easy to find as it aligns with a line drawn between two bright stars of the Ursa Major constellation : Merak and Dubhe (the two stars forming the end of the Big Dipper).

Due to its position seemingly aligned with the Earth's axis of rotation, the apparent position of the Polaris remains constant. It is always observable in the same direction for inhabitants of the northern hemisphere. When observed from the North Pole, it is directly overhead, while if observed from a region close to the equator, it appears closer to the horizon.
name: North Star
trivia: Polaris is actually a multiple-star system comprising 5 stars, of which the brightest component, Ursae Minoris A, is the one visible to the naked eye.

description: RCW 38 is a nebula associated with a star cluster in the Vela constellation. The molecular cloud has a mass of more than 30,000 solar masses and is in the process of creating a huge stellar cluster that already contains about 10,000 stars and protostars, including about 20 massive stars, all in a cube the size of a few light-years across. Although these first stars are less than a million years old and starting to shine and tear through the cloud, most still lie deep in the heart of the cloud and are therefore invisible on the image. We can see dark areas where the gas is not heated yet and remains cold, more or less bright areas in red/orange depending on the amount of energy received by the gas from stars and protostars.
name: RCW 38
trivia: When the first stars formed, the first coyotes appeared on Earth.

description: Regulus is the main star of the Leo constellation and also the 21st brightest star in the sky. It shares similar characteristics with Epsilon Lyrae as it is home to a 4-star system made of two pairs. The stars are named Regulus A, B, C and D. Regulus A is the leader both in terms of mass - 4 solar masses - and size - 4 solar diameters. Whereas the pair Regulus BC orbits around itself and around Regulus A, recent results carried out with a Gaia telescope showed that Regulus D, despite its visual proximity, is in fact a background star located 420 light-years beyond Regulus A.
name: Regulus
trivia: - Regulus A is a fa rotating star that belongs to the blue subgiant stellar category, stars with a well-known light spectrum. Using the Bernard Lyot telescope at Pic du Midi (France) and the Canada-France-Hawaii Telescope at Mauna Kea, some astronomers performed a spectrum of Regulus A and compared it to ones of similar stars. Results confirmed that a potential companion is orbiting around Regulus A, probably a white-dwarf 12 times lighter. Previous studies had shown that the orbital period of this hypothetical neighbor is about 40 days.

description: Rho Oph is a visual binary star located in the Serpentarius constellation. The two stars in this system (Rho Oph A and Rho Oph B) are separated by about 350 times the distance Earth-Sun and take 2,400 years to orbit each other. Rho Oph is surrounded in the sky by Rho Oph C, at 17,000 times the distance Earth-Sun, and another binary system, Rho Oph DE, at 19,000 times the distance Earth-Sun. These stars are part of the star-forming region in the Rho Ophiuchi Molecular Cloud known as IC 4604. Using data from the Gaia satellite, at least 427 stars under 7 million years old have been detected in this region and 41 of them are surrounded by a disk of dust and gas in which planets can form.
name: Rho Ophiuchi
trivia:
2,400 years ago, humanity was in the Bronze Age. The Rho Oph A and Rho Oph B stars were just beginning a new year of orbiting each other.Rho Oph A is approaching us at a speed of 3,600 km/h, the speed of the fastest plane ever built, the Lockheed SR-71 Blackbird.
A 2018 study revealed that Rho Oph A has a magnetic field on its surface. This field could create a spot (like a sunspot) on the star’s surface, which would explain the variation in X-ray emissions.

description: Rigel, also known as Beta Orionis, is the brightest star in the Orion constellation and the 7th brightest in the night sky. Although it is actually a star system of at least three stars, the name Rigel only officially applies to the system’s main star, Beta Ori A. It is an 8 million-year-old massive blue supergiant star. Its mass is 17 times that of the Sun and its radius 80 times. Its surface temperature is twice as high as the Sun's and its luminosity is 40,000 times brighter. In a few million years, Rigel will evolve into a red supergiant, like Betelgeuse, before dying in a supernova explosion.
name: Beta Orionis
trivia:
Rigel's radiation is so powerful, it illuminates the Witch Head Nebula (NGC 1909), a nearby reflection nebula in the galaxy, but is contained in the Eridanus constellation in our night sky.

Rigel 7 is a fictional planet in the Simpsons TV series. It is the home planet of the Rigellians, the most famous members of which are Kang and Kodos, the green aliens who regularly appear in the series.

description:
Sirius also know as the Dog Star is the brightest star in the constellation of Canis Major. With a magnitude of -1.46, it is also the brightest star in the night sky. It holds this record because it is very close to the sun (8.6 light-years away). In addition to its brightness, the star is easy to spot in the sky as it aligns with the three stars of Orion's belt.

Sirius is actually a double star. Sirius B, the companion to the star visible to the naked eye, is a white dwarf with a magnitude of 8.4. The two stars orbit each other in a period of just over 50 years.
name: Sirius
trivia: Although Sirius is the brightest star in the sky, for observers in the northern hemisphere, it appears low on the horizon. Due to atmospheric absorption that diminishes its brightness, it seems less prominent in the sky than the star Arcturus.

description: The 6th planet from the Sun is Saturn, a gas giant with a diameter of 9 times the size of Earth, without counting the rings. It takes Saturn 29 years to orbit the sun, and just 10 hours to rotate on itself. Being a gas giant, Saturn can not support life, but one of its 83 moons may be able to.
name: Saturn
trivia:
- The Cassini spacecraft orbited Saturn 294 times between 2004 and 2017, before intentionally vaporizing in the planet's atmosphere.

- In 2020, Saturn has a total of 83 discovered moons.

description: The Tulip Nebula, also known as Sharpless 101, is an emission nebula located in the constellation Cygnus, a region particularly rich in nebulae. It is found about 6000 light-years away from Earth, extending over a diameter of about 70 light-years, 3 times larger than the best known Orion nebula.
name: Tulip Nebula
trivia: - The HDE 227018 star, in the center of the nebula, feeds the emission of this immense luminescent cloud of gas and interstellar dust.

description: Sharpless 2-106 or Sh 2-106, popularly known as the Celestial Snow Angel, is a so-called bipolar nebula in the northern constellation Cygnus (The Swan) discovered by German astronomer Rudolph Minkowski in 1946. Its wings are twin lobes of super-heated gas emitted from the poles of a young star with a mass 15 times that of our Sun at the centre, surrounded by a ring of dust and gas. Astronomers believe that Sh 2-106 is about 2,000 light-years from Earth, where its apparent size of 3' suggests an actual width of 2 light-years.
name: Celestial Snow Ange
trivia: The central star of the Celestial Snow Angel has a surface temperature of about 36,700 °C.

description: Sharpless 2-140 or Sh2-140 is an emission nebula and open cluster in the constellation Cepheus (The King), best viewed from high latitudes of the Northern Hemisphere. The region is partly obscured by a dark nebula of dust and gas known as LDN 1204, the southwestern edge of which glows brightly due to the ionising effects of a nearby double star. Astronomers believe that Sh2-140 lies about 2,900 light-years from Earth, and its apparent size of 35' implies an actual width of almost 30 light-years.
name: SH2-140
trivia: Sharpless 2-140 is part of the so-called Cepheus Bubble, a 390 light-year-wide shell of dust and gas.

description: The Cave Nebula, also known as Sh2-155 and Caldwell 9, is a diffuse emission and reflection nebula in the Cepheus constellation. Gas from the molecular cloud was blown and compressed by the supernova explosions that occurred in the nearby Cepheus OB3 star association. Currently, the edges of this gigantic molecular structure are being heated, ionized, and illuminated by the massive stars HD 217086 and HD 217061 located next to it. The result is more or less intensely red structures on the image. The deep black regions correspond to the gases and dust in the hidden regions of the cloud that are not affected by neighboring stars. From the gas of the cloud, this region of the galaxy is currently forming new stars in three protoclusters.
name: Cave Nebula
trivia: The Cep OB3b stellar structure containing HD 217086 is 4 million years old and has already formed 3,000 stars. When the stars formed, the first modern versions of elephants, giraffes, zebras, and rhinoceros roamed the savannas on Earth.

description: Sharpless 2-170 or Sh2-170, commonly known as the Little Rosette, is an emission nebula and embedded open cluster in the constellation Cassiopeia (The Seated Queen), best seen from high latitudes of the Northern Hemisphere. As its nickname suggests, Sh2-170 resembles a smaller version of the Rosette Nebula (Caldwell 49). The open cluster at the heart of Sh2-170 is called Stock 18 and lies 9,000 light-years from Earth. Since the apparent size of the surrounding nebulosity is 18', the actual size of the Little Rosette is about 47 light-years.
name: Little Rosette
trivia: The stars in Stock 18 at the centre of the Little Rosette Nebula are about 6 million years old.

description: The Snowman is an emission nebula located 6,000 light-years from Earth, in the Puppis constellation. It is crossed by dark lanes of obscuring dust which gives it the shape of a snowman dressed with a scarf around the neck. It owes its gas cloud to the open star cluster Bochum 5.
name: Snowman Nebula
trivia: Although it is difficult to capture, there is a very small blue reflection nebula, vdB 97, near what could be compared to the snowman's nose.

description: Tarazed is the proper name of Gamma Aquilae, a naked-eye star that, for Northern Hemisphere observers, lies the width of a thumb at arm's length to the upper-right of Altair, the brightest in the constellation Aquila (The Eagle). Despite its Bayer classification of Gamma, magnitude 2.7 Tarazed is the second-brightest star in Aquila. Compared to our Sun, Tarazed is 3.5 times as massive, is 100 times larger, and is around 2500 times more luminous. Some 270 million years old, it will eventually become a white dwarf. Tarazed lies about 395 light-years from Earth.
name: Tarazed
trivia: Tarazed is so large that it is resolvable as a disc from Earth.

description:
T Coronae Borealis is a recurrent variable nova star in the Boreal Crown constellation.It is located approximately 2,630 light years from Earth.
This star is particularly famous for its spectacular, recurring eruptions. The first documented eruption was observed by Irish astronomer John Birmingham in 1866, and the second major eruption occurred in 1946. During these events, the brightness of the star increased dramatically, going from a magnitude of 10 to 2 in a few days, representing a gain in brightness of about 1500 times.
name: T Coronae Borealis
trivia: Due to its impressive eruptions, T Coronae Borealis is sometimes called the Blaze star of the Northern Crown, attracting the attention of amateur and professional astronomers worldwide when it shines exceptionally bright. This phenomenon is estimated to occur approximately every 80 years.

description: The Sun is the central star of our planetary system. At a distance of 149 000 000 km from Earth, the light emitted takes 8 minutes to reach us. With a diameter of 1 392 684 km, the fastest train would complete the travel in 100 days. Aged 4.6 billion years, it is halfway through its life. The core temperature reaches 15 million degrees Celsius while the surface temperature is only 5700 degrees Celsius. The latter temperature is 3 times higher than the temperature required to melt the iron.
name: The Sun

description: Uranus is the 7th planet from the Sun, and takes about 84 years to complete an orbit around our star. Uranus is an ice giant, and cannot support life, as its atmosphere is composed of molecular hydrogen and atomic helium. No spacecraft has ever orbited the ice giant, so it was never studied from up close. Voyager 2 is the only one to achieve a fly-by.
name: Uranus
trivia:
- The moons of Uranus are named after characters from William Shakespeare and Alexander Pope's work.

- Unlike other planets, Uranus rotates on its side.

- The element uranium was named after the ice giant, 8 years after the planet's discovery.

description: Vega, also known as Alpha Lyrae, is the brightest star in the Lyra constellation and the fifth brightest in the night sky. The mass of the star is twice that of the Sun. The star also rotates very fast at a speed of 274 km/s. With that speed of rotation, the centrifugal force flattens the star and gives it an egg shape. Its radius at the equator is 2.78 times that of the Sun, while its polar radius is only 2.26 times that of the Sun. At 400 million years old, the star is much younger than the Sun. The study of its infrared light shows the planet is enveloped by a disk of dust, which could indicate either the disintegration of comets or the explosion of an asteroid.
name: Alpha Lyrae
trivia:
Vega is the star that serves as a baseline for calibrating UBV photometric systems. Indeed, when creating this technique to classify the stars according to their color, the zero points of the B-V and U-B color indexes were defined to be zero for A0V type stars and Vega was the ideal star to be the universal reference.

For the Romans, Vega disappearing below the horizon marked the beginning of autumn.

In 1936, the perfumer Guerlain used the name of the star for his new product.

In the book Contact by Carl Sagan and its film adaptation, the extraterrestrial messages come from Vega.

In the anime television series Grendizer, also known as Goldorak in France, Actarus and his enemies come from the star Vega.

description: The second planet closest to the Sun is Venus, a hot, volcanic, and very windy place that is about the same size has Earth. The winds on Venus are so strong that hurricanes can go around the entire planet in a matter of just 5 days. Like Mercury, a day on Venus lasts longer than a year.
name: Venus
trivia:
- Scientists believe there was once an ocean on Venus, and several of them will focus on researching signs of now-gone water on the planet.

- Venus spins backwards. The sun rises to the West and sets to the East.

- 40 spacecrafts and counting have been sent on a mission to Venus.
